News.title: Celebrity Traitors LIVE: Fears for James Acaster as TV star calls out cruel omission
News.content:
James Acaster has kept a low profile since leaving the show

The Celebrity Traitors have crowned their winners and even though Traitor Maya Jama was eliminated during the last round table, she has made a donation to her chosen charity

Concern has been raised for Celebrity Traitors star James Acaster after fans of the show say he has been 'erased' from history.

Comedian James had one of the most controversial moments in the show's history after he outed himself as a Traitor at the round table to avoid confrontation from fellow contestants.

Since his exit, James was missing from the Uncloaked series and was barely mentioned during the dramatic finale despite playing a big part in the series.

While Maya Jama has been praised by fans after announcing she has donated to her chosen charity even though she didn't win the show.

"Just donated what I would have won for my chosen charity," Maya, who was eliminated during the final round table, tweeted. "Amazing cause."

The Faithfuls came away with the win, as actor Sebastian Croft and comedian Romesh Ranganathan triumphed after seeing off James Blunt, King Kenny and Leigh Anne Pinnock in the nerve-shredding End Game.

News.title: World's longest underwater railway tunnel will cut 2-hour journey down to 26 minutes
News.content:
World's longest underwater railway tunnel will cut 2-hour journey down to 26 minutes

The £3.2bn Yong-Zhou Railway is expected to be completed in 2028

View 4 Images The entrance of the rapid rescue passage in Zhoushan (Image: VCG via Getty Images)

A two-hour bus journey between a Chinese coastal city and an island archipelago is set to be replaced by a 26-minute train ride under plans for the world's longest high-speed underwater railway tunnel.

‌



‌



The £3.2bn Yong-Zhou Railway will connect Ningbo, south of Shanghai, with Zhoushan, a group of islands off China 's east coast. Completion is expected in 2028, with trains capable of reaching 250 kilometres per hour. For passengers travelling between Ningbo and Zhoushan, that means a journey of just 26 minutes, compared with two hours by bus or up to 90 minutes by car.

‌



The connection will also shorten trips from Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang province, to Zhoushan. That journey is expected to take 77 minutes by rail, rather than the current four-and-a-half hours by bus or two-and-a-half hours by car. The project forms part of plans to create a two-hour commuter belt within the province.

‌



View 4 Images A view of the construction site of Jintang undersea tunnel of Ningbo-Zhousha (Image: China News Service via Getty Images)

Running for 47.8 miles between Ningbo East Station and Zhoushan (Baiquan) Station, the railway will include a 10-mile subsea section. Seven stations are planned: four new ones and three that will be redeveloped. A bridge will also be built to link parts of the archipelago.

The scheme has been years in the making. First proposed in 2005, it received approval from Beijing in 2018, before construction began in November 2022. Investment totals 27bn yuan, approximately £3.2bn.

‌



Beneath the seabed, a 135-metre-long tunnel-boring machine called Yongzhou is carrying out the excavation. Dong Bing, the project's chief mechanical engineer, said in an update that the machine was working approximately 93 metres below the seabed.

View 4 Images Tunnel boring machine Dinghai kicks off excavation works for Jintang (Image: VCG via Getty Images)

‌



Its creators say the large-diameter machine is "more sensitive than humans" at spotting irregularities during excavation. It is designed to drill through mountainous terrain and underground landscapes.

Dong Bing said: "Some problems are impossible to detect through human inspection. You might walk by and everything seems fine, but a second later, a problem arises. The system can also collect data, identify related conditions, and analyze potential causes. This is a huge help for safety."

‌



The machinery can also be adapted to the conditions it encounters, according to Hao Weiqi, deputy director of the High-End Equipment Industry Technology Research Institute at China Railway Construction Corp.

View 4 Images Inside the rapid rescue passage (Image: VCG via Getty Images)

‌

He told Global Times: "We can tailor the machines to specific underground environments, while simultaneously providing integrated solutions that combine equipment, intelligent systems, and technical services throughout the entire construction process."

Article continues below

Once Yongzhou has completed 83% of the excavation, it is due to meet a second tunnel-boring machine, Dinghai. That meeting will bring the tunnel beneath the Ningbo seabed close to its final stage.

News.title: New law for 5 dog breeds takes effect today — owners warned 'don't leave the room'
News.content:
New law for 5 dog breeds takes effect today — owners warned 'don't leave the room'

The new law affecting five dog breeds and around 60,000 dogs is now in place and could lead to a criminal record

View Image From today, nipping to the toilet or for a shower could mean a criminal record for some dog owners

A new law that owners of five dog breeds need to be aware of takes effect today. One dog trainer with 20 years of experience warns that now "simply nipping to the loo could mean breaking the law for some dog owners".

‌



‌



From 1 November 2026, it is illegal to leave a child under 12 in close contact with certain dogs in a private setting without adult supervision. Dog owners affected are those that own dogs which feature on the UK's banned dogs list. While owning these dogs is prohibited, it is possible to obtain a certificate of exemption to keep them, and tens of thousands of them currently reside across the UK.

‌



It is also illegal to sell, abandon, give away or breed from a banned dog. Furthermore, whether your dog is classified as a banned type depends on its physical appearance, rather than its breed or name. Therefore, if authorities determine that your dog matches the characteristics of a banned breed, it may be deemed a banned type. The banned dogs in the UK are:

‌



Pit Bull Terrier

Japanese Tosa

Dogo Argentino

Fila Brasileiro

XL Bully

There are a large number of these dogs living across the UK — the XL Bully was not banned until February 2024, while the remaining breeds were all named in the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991. The XL Bully was held responsible for the deaths of 23 people in the two years preceding the ban, yet fatalities continued even after it came into effect, reports the Express.

By the end of 2024, more than 57,000 were registered with the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), though they were being put down at a rate of more than 100 a month at that time. However, these are not the only prohibited dogs residing in Britain.

‌



According to the UK Parliament website, in 2021 there were 3,655 Pit Bull Terriers listed on the Index of Exempted Dogs, 20 Dogo Argentino dogs and three Japanese Tosa dogs. Owners who hold a certificate of exemption permitting them to keep any of these banned breeds must comply with stringent regulations throughout the dog's entire life. The dogs must be:

neutered

fitted with a microchip

kept on a lead and muzzled at all times when in public

kept in a secure place so it cannot escape

‌



Sharon Bolt, a dog trainer and founder of Good Dogs, said: "Simply nipping to the loo could mean breaking the law for some dog owners! Yes, you read that right! A new legal requirement comes into force on Sunday, 1 November, which says that children under 12 cannot be left in close contact with exempted banned-breed dogs, including XL Bullies, without appropriate adult supervision in their home or garden.

"What this means in everyday life is that if you're at home with your young child and dog and need to pop upstairs, have a shower or even nip to the loo, you can't leave them alone together. You'd need to take your child or dog with you, or make sure they're safely separated."

‌



What happens if you own a banned dog?

If you own a banned dog, the UK Government states that police or local council dog wardens are entitled to seize and detain it, even if it is behaving perfectly safely or no complaints have been made. If the dog is on private property, the police must obtain a warrant to do so.

A police or council dog expert will subsequently assess what breed of dog you own and whether it poses, or could pose, a risk to the public. The dog could then be returned to you, placed in kennels or put down. It is the owner's responsibility to demonstrate that their dog is not a prohibited breed.

Article continues below

Should you succeed in proving this, a court will order the dog's return. If you are unable to prove it, or admit it is a banned breed, you will be convicted of an offence and could face an unlimited fine or imprisonment for up to six months (or both). Your dog will also be destroyed.

News.title: Ten dead and 24 injured after minibus and lorry crash near Cairo in Egypt
News.content:
Ten dead and 24 injured after minibus and lorry crash near Cairo in Egypt

A minibus crash near Cairo has left 10 people dead and 24 injured after the vehicle collided with a heavy truck near 6th of October City in Egypt.

View 2 Images The wreckage of the minibus following the deadly crash near Cairo, Egypt. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

At least 10 people have been died and 24 others injured after a minibus collided with a heavy truck near Cairo.

‌



‌



The crash happened on Saturday near 6th of October City, on the western outskirts of the Egyptian capital, according to Egypt’s health ministry.

‌



Emergency services raced to the intersection of the Middle Ring Road and Dabaa Road in the city, in Giza province, to reports of a crash.

‌



Dozens were then rushed to hospital from the scene.

Officials confirmed 10 people were tragically pronounced dead as a result of the crash. A further 24 people were injured, 10 of whom were in critical condition, the ministry said.

‌



Images from the scene show the extent of the damage as a minibus was seen crumped on the highway.

Health ministry spokesperson Hossam Abdel Ghaffar said the number of casualties are preliminary and that officials are continuing to assess the situation.

‌



View 2 Images The wreckage of the minibus on a highway (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The collision comes as the latest fatal road accident reported in Egypt in recent months, with around 75,000 people injured every year and more than 5,000 deaths reported annually on the roads.

Article continues below

Earlier in October, 13 people died and 34 were injured when a truck collided with a tourist bus west of Cairo. Another crash in the Sinai Peninsula was responsible for the deaths of 22 people, including 10 Jordanian tourists.

In August, 18 people, including children, died when two pick-up trucks transporting agricultural day labourers crashed in northern Egypt.

News.title: BBC dog expert explains what it means if dog wags tail, yawns or looks away
News.content:
BBC dog expert explains what it means if dog wags tail, yawns or looks away

A wagging tail is often seen as a sign of a friendly dog, but dog trainer Sharon Bolt says owners must read the whole body language to stay safe

View Image Dog trainer Sharon Bolt has revealed some key signs your dog might not be as happy as you think (Image: Sharon Bolt)

It might not be immediately apparent to us, but two dogs can stand on opposite sides of a street and hold an entire conversation without uttering a single sound. One glances away and sniffs the ground, while the other stands taller, tenses up and fixes the first dog with an intense stare.

‌



‌



Sharon Bolt, a dog trainer and founder of Good Dogs, says that silent exchange can frequently reveal whether they're attempting to avoid conflict or whether a confrontation may be on the cards.

‌



"I've had the pleasure of working with dogs and their owners for over 20 years, and it's often the smallest changes in a dog's expression or posture that can tell me the most," Sharon told the Express.

‌



"Learning to recognise these signals early gives us the opportunity to understand when our dogs are feeling uncomfortable and take action before a situation escalates into growling, lunging, snapping or biting."

On the day a new law comes into effect affecting five breeds and around 60,000 dogs, Sharon has outlined key canine behaviours that owners may be misreading. Today's legislative change means it is now unlawful to leave a child under 12 in close contact with certain dogs in a private setting without adult supervision.

A wagging tail isn't always friendly

"This is one of the biggest misconceptions I see," says Sharon, who is often heard discussing dogs on BBC radio. "If we take an example of two dogs greeting either visitors or another dog, one could have soft eyes, a relaxed body with their tail moving freely, while the other dog could be holding their body stiffly, their mouth tightly closed with their tail held high and wagging, often with short, rigid movements.

‌



"Although both the dogs' tails are moving, they are feeling very differently. The first dog is happy and relaxed whilst the second dog is giving other signals that indicate that they are feeling tense and that things could escalate. This is why it's really important to read their entire body language rather than just trusting that a wagging tail always means that the dog is happy and friendly.

"And while a stiff, upright body is an important warning, other signals of discomfort can be so subtle they're easily mistaken for something else entirely."

‌



A yawn doesn't always mean 'I'm tired'

"Imagine a visitor bending over a dog to say hello," says Sharon. "Rather than leaning towards them, the dog turns their head away, licks their lips or gives an unexpected yawn. These signs suggest that the close interaction is too much and is making the dog feel uncomfortable.

"These subtle clues are known as calming or appeasement signals. Dogs use them when they're uncomfortable, trying to ease tension with people or other dogs, or to avoid confrontation. They may also blink frequently or move their ears back.

‌



"Of course, dogs yawn when they're tired, just like we do, and they lick their lips around food. That's why we need to look at the full picture of what's going on around them to help us understand what these signals are telling us."

Why grass suddenly becomes fascinating

"On a walk, a dog may suddenly start sniffing the ground as another dog approaches," says Sharon. "They might slow down, lower their body or take a curved path instead of heading straight towards them. Another sign that they might not want to say hello is if they lift their head and deliberately look away.

‌



"Just as some people feel uncomfortable meeting strangers, not all dogs enjoy meeting dogs they don't know. Some are naturally shy or timid, while others have had unpleasant experiences and feel much happier keeping their distance. They may love the company of people and dogs they know, but do not want to necessarily greet every dog they meet.

"These signals are effectively saying, 'No thanks, I don't want to say hello, and I don't want any trouble'. If they're forced into a greeting despite displaying these signs, their discomfort can escalate into growling, lunging or snapping. Giving them more distance or changing direction from the other dog can prevent the confrontation before it occurs."

‌



The 3 Fs for dogs: Flight, Freeze and Fight

"When dogs feel threatened, they have three instinctive responses," Sharon explains. "Their first instinct is to move away from whatever is worrying them (flight). If they can't escape, they will often become completely still (freeze), and if the threat continues, they can resort to barking, lunging, snapping or biting to defend themselves (fight).

"This also helps to explain why some dogs react towards other dogs when they're on the lead but are far more relaxed off it. The lead restricts their ability to move away from the other dog, leaving them feeling trapped and more likely to react defensively. Recognising the signals early means we can create distance before the situation becomes a problem."

Article continues below

A happier, safer life together

"Whether your dog is looking away to avoid an encounter, freezing because they're uncomfortable or reacting because they feel trapped, they're communicating how they feel," says Sharon.

"The more we understand what they're telling us, the easier it becomes to prevent any unwanted confrontations and to enjoy a happier, more relaxed life together."

News.title: New £15 Aldi jacket looks just like £40 Debenhams and £56 Next - in stores now

New £15 Aldi jacket looks just like £40 Debenhams and £56 Next - in stores now

Aldi has added to its clothing range with a jacket that bears a striking resemblance to pricier options elsewhere

View 3 Images The item can only be picked up in-store (Image: Getty Images)

The autumn chill is here, and temperatures will continue to plummet as winter draws near. Shoppers looking for ways to stave off the cold and keep warm may be interested in a new jacket at Aldi that looks eerily similar to higher-end options on sale at rival retailers.

‌



‌



Now available across all 1,000+ stores while stocks last, the Adults Outdoor Sweat Jacket - available in blue, black and brown in sizes medium to extra large - is retailing for £14.99. It can only be picked up in-store, however, which is not good news for people who like home delivery.

‌



At a glance, the jacket has a fleece-like look that will help trap warmth to your body, helped by the zip fastening and hood. There is a front pocket to hold your everyday essentials like phones and wallets, while there's a cool coordinates design on the top left.

‌

News.title: Leftover Halloween pumpkin £50,000 fine warning issued to millions in UK
News.content:
Leftover Halloween pumpkin £50,000 fine warning issued to millions in UK

Experts are warning UK families of dumping leftover pumpkins outdoors

View 3 Images Leftover pumpkin flesh can make hedgehogs, foxes, and other wild animals sick (Image: Getty)

As Halloween festivities draw to a close, waste experts are issuing an urgent warning against carelessly discarding or abandoning pumpkins outdoors. With millions carved throughout the UK annually, families are being urged to rethink conventional disposal practices to safeguard local wildlife and minimise avoidable landfill waste.

‌



‌



An expert is calling on households to pause before dumping their leftover decorations in woodland areas. While leaving a pumpkin outside may appear to be a straightforward way of providing wildlife with a seasonal snack, carved pumpkins can rapidly become a serious health risk.

‌



Dr Sean McCormack, Head Vet at Tails.com, explains why your Halloween pumpkin doesn't belong in the woods. He also explains what to do instead and what dog owners should watch out for.

‌



Why can you be fined and how much?

You could face fines of up to £50,000 for illegally disposing of leftover Halloween pumpkins. While many people assume leaving old pumpkins in woods or parks is a beneficial way to feed local wildlife, it actually poses an environmental hazard, reports the Liverpool Echo.

View 3 Images You can face fines up to £50,000 if you illegally dump leftover Halloween pumpkins in the countryside or public spaces (Image: Getty)

Dumping old pumpkins in woodland, parks or countryside areas is legally regarded as fly-tipping, which can result in an immediate on-the-spot Fixed Penalty Notice of up to £5,000 following recent government clampdowns on waste crime. Should the offence be considered serious enough to be heard in a Magistrates' Court, the financial penalty can rise dramatically to a maximum fine of £50,000, alongside a possible 12-month jail term.

‌



For large-scale or repeated dumping that reaches a Crown Court, offenders face unlimited fines and up to five years behind bars, as local authorities actively deploy CCTV and public tip-offs to catch those abandoning seasonal waste. Leaving a decomposing pumpkin on an ordinary city street can also result in a £150 littering fine.

Beyond public dumping, keeping old pumpkins on your property for too long poses its own legal risks. Leaving soft, decaying pumpkins or Halloween props on your front path, porch or driveway can create serious slipping and tripping hazards.

‌



Under the Occupiers' Liability Act, you have a duty of care towards anyone visiting your property. If a delivery driver, neighbour or visitor is injured by falling over your leftover decorations, you could face civil liability and court fines of up to £5,000. Failing to clear away these hazards can sometimes invalidate your home insurance policy should a claim be made against you.

Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

‌



View 3 Images Throwing them straight into general waste causes them to rot in landfills, releasing methane

Why shouldn't you dump your pumpkin in the woods?

Leftover pumpkin flesh can make hedgehogs, foxes, and other wild animals sick.

Piles of rotting pumpkin attract rodents like rats and spread bacteria that disrupt local woodland and park soils.

Throwing them straight into general waste causes them to rot in landfills, releasing methane.

‌



A decomposing pumpkin attracts pests such as rats and introduces bacteria that can disrupt the natural equilibrium of woodland and park soils. Pumpkin flesh can also pose serious risks to wildlife, acting as a powerful laxative for hedgehogs and causing life-threatening dehydration during a crucial period when they need to build up weight ahead of winter hibernation.

The RSPB and regional wildlife trusts, including the Cornwall Wildlife Trust, frequently issue warnings that pumpkin flesh can cause severe stomach problems and fatal dehydration in hedgehogs, preventing them from gaining the weight needed for winter hibernation.

‌



Dr Sean McCormack said: "Once Halloween is over, it can seem more environmentally friendly to leave your pumpkin in a local woodland than to put it in the bin. You might think you're providing a free meal for wildlife and letting the pumpkin naturally decompose, but that doesn't mean it's the best thing for the animals living there.

Starbucks pumpkin spice latte all-year-round hack

‌



"Leaving food in natural habitats can encourage wildlife to gather in places they wouldn't usually feed and can interfere with their normal foraging behaviour. Rotting food can also attract pests and other animals, so even though you're trying to do something positive, you're still introducing something into that environment that wouldn't naturally be there in that quantity.

"There's also a big difference between a fresh pumpkin and one that's spent days or weeks sitting on a doorstep. By the end of October, your carved pumpkin may have been exposed to rain, fluctuating temperatures, insects and bacteria, and once it begins to break down, it can quickly become mouldy. Rather than taking your pumpkin somewhere else to decompose, dispose of it responsibly at home."

‌



What are the safe ways to dispose of leftover pumpkin?

Chop them up and put them in your garden compost bin.

Place them in your local council food waste or brown bin.

Use the flesh for cooking or leave seeds out for birds.

Chucking pumpkins straight into your general household rubbish bin means they'll end up buried in landfill, where they'll decompose without oxygen and release methane, an extremely damaging greenhouse gas. To dispose of your Halloween pumpkins safely and avoid the risk of a fine, you should use official waste channels or use your own garden.

‌



The most effective option is to chop the pumpkin into smaller chunks and pop it straight into your home garden compost bin, where it can break down naturally. If you don't compost at home, put the pumpkin in your local council food waste bin or brown garden recycling bin, according to your local authority's particular guidelines.

Alternatively, if the pumpkin remains fresh and hasn't been carved or left outdoors to decay, you can utilise the flesh for autumn recipes or roast the seeds to put out as a safe snack for garden birds.

Article continues below

Freshly cut, uncarved pumpkin flesh can be roasted and blitzed into a smooth puree for pumpkin bread, stirred into a warming lentil soup, or mixed directly into pancake batter for a festive breakfast. The seeds can be rinsed, dried, and tossed with oil or butter and spices like cinnamon or garlic powder to create a crunchy, oven-roasted snack.

News.title: Octopus Energy and OVO free heated throws for winter 2026 - who qualifies
News.content:
Octopus Energy and OVO free heated throws for winter 2026 - who qualifies

Thousands of households can get help with paying their energy bills - including free heated throws and electric blankets

View 3 Images Using a heated throw means you might be able to save on heating your home (Image: Getty)

Energy firms have confirmed they are continuing with schemes to help some customers who are struggling with their bills - including giving away items they say can save money while keeping people warm. Both Octopus Energy and OVO have offers to help ranging from free home emergency kits to heated throws.

‌



‌



Octopus confirmed this month it will be running its free electric throw scheme again in 2026 alongside its heated throws scheme which it says can help keep warm without heating the whole house. It explains: "Our heated throws scheme is there to support customers most in need, particularly people with really specific vulnerabilities and medical needs. To make sure the blankets are getting into the right hands, we’ll be prioritising those customers."

‌



View 3 Images Making the swap could be one way to help lower energy bills (Image: Getty )

‌



It added: "If you can, do think about buying a heated throw yourself. They tend to cost around £40, and our research shows the typical home could save £300 by using a heated throw to keep warm rather than always heating the whole house."

The firm explained: "One of our boffins realised that some customers were paying to heat their entire homes, even if they lived alone. He did some calculations and found out that where heating a whole home cost about £4 a day, an energy-efficient heated throw could heat a person for just 2-4p an hour.

"This means an heated throw is a vastly more cost-effective way to stay warm: particularly for people with mobility issues, for example, and those who spend a lot of time in one spot. Or those with medical issues that mean they feel the cold more, or are more prone to illness.

‌



"Modern heated throws, used according to their instructions, are safe and energy efficient. We use our purchasing power to buy tens of thousands and offer them for free to customers we identify will benefit most when they fill in our financial assistance tool. So far, as of August 2026, we've given out more than 110,000!"

Ensure our latest (fill in the details here such as home and technology) headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings

‌



The firm explained how it decided who qualified for one of the free throws or blankets. It said: "We’ve been really trying to target people who need a blanket most, so we haven’t offered one to every customer, and we've tried to keep it to one per home so that we can support as many people as possible."

And it said there could be savings of hundreds of pounds a year. It advised: "We've run some analysis on customers who got a heated throw and found that they saved up to 10-20% on their bills on average in the winter months after getting their blanket. Over a year, that’s a massive £300 saving."

‌



Octopus Energy said it is offering heated throws to the most vulnerable homes. It is one electric heated throw per household; this is so we can help as many people as possible. It also has a range of other money saving and financial aid schemes available. It says the first step is to apply to the Octo Assist fund.

View 3 Images Energy giant OVO also has schemes to help (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile OVO Extra Support aims to help customers who need some additional help to manage and pay for their energy. It said: "Whether you've had a change in your circumstances or an ongoing need, we are here to help wherever we can."

It said its Energy Saving Support scheme offers help "from free home efficiency kits, to heated throws". It added: "We can help to give you tailored advice and support as well as funding options to help reduce your energy costs ongoing."

‌



Under its Direct Financial Support schemes e ligible customers may qualify for direct financial support towards their energy bill or to support existing energy debt. There is also specialist debt and benefits advice to help people maximise their income.

It said if people are stuggling then they can make a quick check and get an immediate answer. It added: " If you think you’ll struggle to pay your bills and you’re an OVO customer, then you might be eligible. It doesn’t take long to apply for support and you’ll get your answer right away.

Article continues below

"When you apply for support, things like household income, any disposable income, and medical needs will be taken into account – to help prioritise those who need help most. We won’t be able to offer everything to everyone - but we’re hoping to help as many people as possible. Our specialist teams will be available to speak to any of our customers who are worried about energy costs."

OVO customers can check their eligibility here.

News.title: Emotional reunions for Oleshky evacuees after years in Russia-occupied city
News.content:
People evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky were reunited with their loved ones after crossing from Belarus into Ukraine on Saturday.

This comes as a ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump took effect across the frontline region of Kherson on Tuesday.

Families were reunited at a site in the region of Chernihiv in northern Ukraine after arriving in buses and ambulances.

They had previously travelled via Crimea and Russia after their evacuation from the Ukrainian town on Friday.

Ceasefire measures will remain in place until the end of Sunday 1 November.

The BBC's Dan Johnson reports from the site in the Chernihiv region, near the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus.

News.title: Democrats are used to heartbreak in Texas - could Talarico turn the tide?
News.content:
The race for a US Senate seat in Texas may prove crucial in determining which party controls Congress next year â a significant prize in its own right - but for both parties it represents so much more than that.

For the Democrats, their losing streak in statewide elections now stretches back more than three decades. In the second most populous state in America, liberals have been in the wilderness for a generation.

But polls suggest their candidate, 37-year-old James Talarico, may be on the verge of breaking through and turning a Texas Senate seat blue for the first time since 1988.

That would be a dream scenario for Democrats - and a potential nightmare for Republicans.

"If the Democrats do pull it off, I think it's going to cause a lot of soul searching and a lot of psychological damage to the Republican Party in Texas and nationwide," said Brendan Steinhauser, a Texas-based Republican campaign strategist.

These dramatic stakes help explain how this Senate race has rocketed to become the most expensive in US history, with total spending reaching more than half a billion dollars.

For Talarico, it has been a remarkable rise for a candidate who in 2025 was a relatively unknown state-level Democrat.

At the Fiesta Center in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday night, the line to see the softly spoken former teacher, who studied to be a Christian minister, stretched around the building and down the wide parking lot to a busy road.

In this dusty western plains town of about 250,000, which voted overwhelmingly for President Donald Trump two years ago, a visit from a major Democratic candidate on the eve of an election was unusual.

"It's just so amazing to watch," said Aaron Gonzalez, the Democratic Party chair for Hockley County, which borders Lubbock. "This time is different."

News.title: Reeves says UK's future should be inside the EU
News.content:
Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves has argued the UK's future should be inside the EU, and that Brexit has made the country "poorer, weaker and less secure".

In her first major intervention since leaving the Treasury, Reeves said she welcomed debate around the UK's relationship with Europe.

At the last election, Labour's manifesto said a Labour government would stay outside the EU and make Brexit work.

But Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there needs to be an honest discussion about what the future relationship looks like.

The Conservatives have said there is no desire to rerun the Brexit debate and Reform UK's Nigel Farage has said there is no mandate to pursue closer EU ties.

Labour's 2024 election manifesto ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.

Burnham has said that any changes would require a mandate at a general election, which is next due by 2029.

In the Sunday Times, external, Reeves wrote: "No-one in the Treasury ever doubted where my instincts were. I do believe Britain's future lies in the European Union."

She said supporters of rejoining the EU had to "make the argument, demonstrate tangible benefits and to get the next steps right".

Reeves added that at the forthcoming UK-EU summit, she hoped for confirmation of the youth mobility scheme she has been pushing for since she was in office.

She also said she was hoping for "progress towards entry" into the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) scheme.

Announced last March, SAFE is part of an EU-wide effort to rearm after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

A defence pact agreed with the EU last May paved the way for UK-based defence companies to be part of projects funded by SAFE.

In her piece for the Sunday Times, Reeves also sought to defend her record in office.

She wrote about the need for governments to be "braver" in building big infrastructure projects and "clear eyed" about the risks and benefits AI would drive in advanced economies.

News.title: Who are the real winners of Celebrity Traitors?
News.content:
Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from The Celebrity Traitors final

In some ways, all the players on The Celebrity Traitors can be seen as winners.

They all got to appear on a hugely popular TV show, rubbing shoulders with other stars and gaining new fans along the way.

But there are certain celebrities, such as Miranda Hart, King Kenny, Maya Jama and Joanne McNally, who have been tipped by industry experts as getting the biggest career boost after the show.

Sebastian "Bash" Croft - who won the game, alongside Romesh Ranganathan - could also now be in line for greater roles.

We've taken a look at the breakout stars of the series and what might lie ahead for them.

News.title: Watch: Heidi Klum as giant severed hand for Halloween bash
News.content:
The supermodel and TV host Heidi Klum continued her pose as the queen of Halloween by transforming into a giant, bloodied and severed hand for her annual costume party on 31 October.

Klum, 53, was completely unrecognisable arriving at her event in what she described as her own chopped-off "left hand".

This year was the 25th anniversary of the party, which has provided viral pop culture moments over the years, like when Klum dressed up as a worm in 2022.

News.title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests
News.content:
When Lisa Clewes returned to her Welsh holiday let after a group of guests checked out, she was horrified by the mess.

Just days earlier, she had met the group in person and helped with their luggage.

But after a dinner party, the house was left "in a complete mess" with broken glasses, drinks cans on the floor, pans full of food on the table and fish guts left in the garden.

"It was really unbelievable. Had I had another booking the same day, I would have had to cancel or delay check-in," says Clewes.

She charges a cleaning fee that covers around 75% of the cost of a cleaner and asks guests to empty the fridge, put rubbish in the bins and load the dishwasher.

News.title: I've been stuck on a tiny Pacific island for years and can't get a transit visa to fly home to Sri Lanka
News.content:
When Ruchira Ranasingha left Sri Lanka almost a decade ago, she could never have imagined she would end up stranded on a tiny archipelago in the South Pacific.

The 50-year-old has now been stuck in the Cook Islands for three years. She tells the BBC she is desperate to go back to Sri Lanka and has even offered to go "handcuffed, bound and gagged".

Ranasingha had been hoping to settle in New Zealand.

After seeking asylum there, she says she followed an immigration adviser's recommendation to temporarily exit the country to apply for a work visa. But once in the Cook Islands, her application was rejected. And by leaving New Zealand, she had breached the terms of her existing asylum-linked visa.

Now New Zealand is refusing to issue her a transit visa that would allow her to fly home to Sri Lanka.

Australia is refusing too. The only other international destinations she can fly to from the Cook Islands - Tahiti and Hawaii - require her to give biometric information in New Zealand before any visa can be processed.

As a result, she has no feasible way of leaving.

"My son - my only child - is getting married in November and I really want to be there for his wedding. My mother is so worried about what has happened to me that she is constantly in and out of hospital," she says through tears.

"I will do anything they ask of me - I just want to go home."

News.title: From Maya as Sir Mo Farah to Heidi as her own left hand: The best Halloween looks
News.content:
Supermodel and TV host Heidi Klum confirmed her position as the queen of Halloween by transforming into a giant, bloodied and severed hand for her annual costume party in New York.

Klum, 53, was completely unrecognisable arriving at her event in what she described as her own chopped-off "left hand".

This year marks the 25th anniversary of Klum's party, which brings celebrities across the globe together dressed in their wild, weird and wonderful costumes.

And the revelry didn't stop there, with celebrities such as Maya Jama wowing attendees at her own Halloween party in London dressed as four-time Olympic champion Sir Mo Farah.

News.title: Healey risks breaking minimum wage promise for younger workers
News.content:
The Chancellor, John Healey, has suggested that younger workers might not receive the same minimum wage as others before the next election, potentially breaking a Labour manifesto promise.

In 2024, Labour said it would remove "discriminatory age bands", vowing to end the gap between the adult minimum wage and pay for 18 to 20-year-olds.

But in last week's Budget, Healey said that younger workers would see the same increase as older workers, leaving a gap between the two rates this year.

Pay for 18 to 20-year-olds in 2026 will rise to Â£11.27, while over-20s will be paid a minimum of Â£13.21 an hour.

In a BBC interview to be broadcast on Sunday, Healey was asked if younger workers would be paid the same as older workers, when it comes to the minimum wage, by the time of the next election?

"We'll take one step at a time," he said, suggesting that Labour might abandon its plan to close the gap before the next election.

It is a change that is likely to anger the unions and some on the left of the party.

Healey added that Labour was still committed to the ambition, but hinted the plan to equalise wages might be delayed, partly to encourage businesses to employ younger workers.

"There is no question about whether or if, it's a question of when - it's a question of how fast," he said.

"I want to make sure we can look hard at those trade-offs that are there between jobs and wages."

"I want to take business, I want to take trade unions with me, and with the government, because together we have to get into what at the moment is a moral shame on this nation. A million youngsters - written off without any prospect of being helped into work and making contributions to this country for the future."

News.title: King to address slavery during Commonwealth speech in Antigua on final leg of Caribbean tour
News.content:
King Charles III is to speak with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" on the lasting pain of the transatlantic slave trade, during the final leg of his Caribbean tour in Antigua, Buckingham Palace has said.

The King will address Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday in a speech which will touch on the issue.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier he was "open" to the possibility of the UK formally apologising for its role in slavery - a change in the government's stance.

It is understood the Palace was told in advance of Burnham's comments in an opinion piece on Friday night, and the King has not made any changes to his speech in light of them.

The British government has never formally apologised for slavery or offered to pay reparations.

Burnham has previously stuck with the policy of his predecessors, and stopped short of offering any consideration of reparation payments.

The King will make his speech at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).

He "will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this visit", a Palace spokesperson said.

"You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow, and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue at CHOGM and beyond."

When asked about the King's reaction to the prime minister's comments, the spokesperson said it would "not be appropriate" for the King to address matters of policy relating to "the UK Government's position".

The Caribbean tour has again thrust King Charles into the difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.

On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech where he spoke of the "suffering of the past".

In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.

Buckingham Palace said it was a moment for the King to learn more about the history of slavery and resistance. His engagements have also covered the environment, opportunities for young people and trade relationships with the UK.

News.title: Hamilton takes first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City Grand Prix
News.content:
Russell, who said he was happy to have ended a run of difficult form but could not explain why, took a unilateral decision not to do a preparation lap after his out lap on his final run.

He said he had a "gut feeling" that it was the best approach, but the team had insisted on a prep lap and had fuelled the car for the extra mileage.

"[The time loss for the extra fuel weight is] such a small number," said Russell, "but it's bigger than the gap to pole. Nevertheless, I'm just happy to be up here."

Verstappen said traffic with another car is what led to his loss of time.

"Already going into (Turn) 12 I had a car very close to me and I already lost time there with the dirty air," he said.

"And then going into the hairpin, instead of going on the left, I had one car on my right where you normally want to open up the corner. So its a bit of an awkward angle you have to go into the hairpin.

"Plus you lose your reference on the right-hand side where you are constantly looking. It's a difficult corner to get right, that killed my lap. The most promising thing is how we turned it around as in practice I was not that happy and we turned it around, I was in the fight for pole."

McLaren's Lando Norris had looked in contention for pole, fastest in the second session and on the first runs in the final session, when he was third fastest behind Leclerc and Verstappen.

But he failed to improve on his final lap and had to be satisfied fight sixth.

"Just not quick enough that's all," said Norris. "The lap was incredible in Q2 to put me P1. That was very unrealistic in terms of achieving that again in Q3.

"I am pretty happy with P6, can't ask a lot more and pretty happy with the job I did with the car I have."

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls pair Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Pierre Gasly completed the top 10.

Lawson was later disqualified from qualifying for an Infringement of the technical regulations regarding the usage of the electrical deployment of the power unit and will start from the back.

Fernando Alonso looked to be in contention for his best qualifying of the year for Aston Martin when he went fastest on his first lap of the session ahead of a number of cars that for most of the season have been ahead of him.

But his engine suffered a water leak in the energy recovery system as he started his second attempt, when he was still lying third, and he was ordered to stop the car on track.

Alonso's frustration after a year of poor performance and reliability from the Honda engine was clear in an interview with the official television channel afterwards, when he said a total of nine words in answer to four questions.

In those words, he confirmed it had been an engine problem, said "it was" a good opportunity and it was "correct" that the car has been looking good all weekend - but that he could not do anything in the race "from the back".

News.title: Thick fog to create hazardous driving conditions into next week
News.content:
Dense fog will blanket parts of the UK on Sunday and into next week, causing dangerous driving conditions.

England and Wales are most likely to experience the foggy conditions on Sunday, before the threat shifts northwards into next week.

It comes after the Met Office issued a yellow weather warning for parts of England and Wales early on Saturday morning and again on Sunday morning with visibility on roads less than 100m in places.

Further warnings could be issued in the coming days as the waning strength of the late autumn sun means mist, fog and patches of low cloud are slow to clear.

News.title: Second night of drone disruption at Jersey Airport
News.content:
People at Jersey Airport have said they are frustrated and angry that "unauthorised drone" activity caused more flight cancellations for a second night in a row.

At 20:05 on Saturday Jersey Airport said it was "experiencing disruption.... affecting inbound flights as a result of further drone activity in the vicinity of the airfield".

States of Jersey Police are investigating the incidents and officers have appealed to anyone with information about who is responsible to come forward.

Insp Rob McCallum said it was believed "two or three" drones had entered the restricted airspace, but they were not thought to be linked to terrorism.

News.title: Europe can no longer rely on US to 'bankroll' its defence, Starmer says
News.content:
Sir Keir Starmer has said Europe should build a common security framework, warning the change in its defence relationship with the US is permanent rather than "an aberration of the Trump presidency".

The former prime minister was speaking at a British Irish Chamber of Commerce (BICC) dinner in Dublin, external on Friday evening.

Sir Keir said a "common security framework" for Europe was needed as much as a common market, with the UK at its centre.

He warned that "things will not go back to the way they were," adding that the US had made clear it will no longer "bankroll" its European allies.

Press Association reported that he told the crowd in Dublin City Hall his comments did not mean "the US relationship is no longer important".

Rather he said the UK-USA military, security and intelligence alliance was "far too strong for that".

But he said Europe must be enabled to "take on far more responsibility for its own defence and security".

"Europe has twice been caught asleep â failing to anticipate and prepare for predictable events," he said.

"First when Russia's attack on Ukraine exposed long-standing European weaknesses on defence and security; and second when President Trump made clear, once and for all, that the US will no longer bankroll our European security. We have to catch up," he added.

He added: "I will say here what I have said to European leaders. This is about responding to a permanent change of affairs, not an aberration of the Trump presidency. Things will not go back to the way they were before.

Sir Keir was at the dinner to be awarded an honorary life membership from the BICC.

News.title: 'It's been killing me!' Celebrity Traitors winners relieved the secret is out
News.content:
Spoiler warning: This story reveals details of The Celebrity Traitors final

The winners of Celebrity Traitors have said they are relieved that they no longer need to keep the biggest secret in British TV, as they reunited to celebrate their victory.

Actor Sebastian Croft and comedian Romesh Ranganathan were the last ones standing, with the two faithfuls splitting the Â£83,000 prize pot between their chosen charities.

"I am feeling good, it's so nice to finally be able to talk about it properly," Croft, known to pals as Bash, told BBC Newsbeat.

The second series of the hit BBC One show finished on Friday, after the original 21 celebs were whittled down to seven finalists.

Reuniting with Ranganathan on the comedian's BBC Radio 2 show on Saturday morning, Croft said they had been worried about being seen together in public before the final.

"We were having dinner and we're not exactly a likely duo and the whole restaurant was like, 'we like you on Traitors and hope you win'," he said.

Croft added that he had woken up on Saturday "with a light sense that I don't have to keep the secret anymore. It's been killing me".

Ranganathan, 48, started his show by saying: "Last night, I don't know if you're aware, was the finale of The Celebrity Traitors and I won."

He said he was "delighted to win" but admitted he probably wouldn't have done so without Croft convincing him to banish the last remaining traitor, King Kenny.

"It's taken the gloss off it slightly that everybody's saying, 'you better thank [Croft] every day for the rest of your life'," he added, with his typical deadpan-humour.

But 24-year-old Croft said he thought Ranganathan had played the game in a "lovely" way.

"People are seeing how smart you are and how you're actually so on it, and you're such a good judge of character," he praised.

News.title: Fireworks and fancy dress at Derry's 40th Halloween festival
News.content:
The 40th anniversary of Londonderry's Halloween festival has come to a spectacular close, with a carnival parade and fireworks display lighting up the skies over the River Foyle.

From its humble beginnings in the 1980s, the festival has grown to become what organisers have called Europe's largest Halloween celebration.

This year, Derry marked four decades of the festival with events inspired by folklore, mythology and the traditions of Samhain, the ancient Celtic festival from which Halloween has its roots.

Now a major fixture in the city's calendar, the final day of the festival attracted visitors from around the world, who joined in the celebrations with all of the ghosts, ghouls and goblins.

News.title: Brian May reveals the Neil Armstrong remark that ‘petrified’ him
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Queen legend Sir Brian May has recalled the moment Neil Armstrong responded to a speech he made about human exploration in space, while lamenting what he perceives as a lack of “decent” billionaires.

The revered guitarist gave a notable speech in 2011 in which he questioned the idea of humans venturing beyond Earth “when we’ve made such a mess of our own planet”.

Sitting in the audience were six Apollo moonwalkers including Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin, who were the first men to walk on the moon, as well as Charlie Duke and Harrison Schmitt from the Apollo 16 and Apollo 17 missions.

“I wish I could find a billionaire who was a decent human being,” May, 79, told EL PAÍS at Starmus, the music, science and philosophy festival he hosts in Spain’s Canary Islands.

“They all seem to be fostering their own selfish interests while the world falls apart: they’re destroying it, people are suffering. That’s more important than going to space.”

He continued: “The first time I gave a speech about why we should be in space, I said: ‘Why do we feel confident, worthy, to be putting our seed into space when we’ve made such a mess of our own planet?’”

open image in gallery May said he was nervous after giving a speech about space exploration in front of Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin ( AFP/Getty )

May admitted he was “petrified, terrified” to make those remarks in front of Armstrong and his peers: “I thought I might be saying maybe we shouldn’t go to space, in front of those who pioneered it, and that they would hate me.”

To his surprise and relief, Armstrong came up to him after he left the stage and apparently said: “You said the right thing.”

The journalist noted that the exploration of space had shifted from “a matter of nations and science” to “private companies and billionaires”, as hugely wealthy and controversial individuals such as Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk.

This week, Russian president Vladimir Putin called Musk, founder and CEO of aerospace manufacturer SpaceX, a “real genius” after revealing he and Musk are in “close” contact about satellite technology.

open image in gallery Putin (right) called SpaceX owner a ‘real genius’, weeks after Ukraine complained of speed restrictions hampering its ability to intercept Russian attack drones. Neither Musk or the US government have taken responsibility for imposing speed curbs ( AFP/Getty )

Speaking at the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, Putin said it was important for Russia to be in contact with Musk so Russia’s satellite project, Rassvet, and SpaceX’s Starlink did not “interfere with each other in orbit”.

His comments came just weeks after Ukraine, which uses a military version of Starlink, named Starshield, as a crucial component of its drone operations and battlefield communications, complained of speed restrictions hampering its ability to intercept Russian attack drones.

Neither Musk nor the US government, which operates Starshield using Starlink technology, have taken responsibility for imposing the speed curbs.

Meanwhile, Amazon billionaire Bezos received criticism last year for his highly publicised Blue Origin NS-31 mission, in which six all-female crew members including pop star Katy Perry and Bezos’s wife, Lauren Sanchez, for an 11-minute space flight.

While the mission was billed as a historic, feminist moment, it was derided by many as a marketing stunt for Bezos’s space tourism business, while others castigated the environmental impact of the trip. Sources later said that Perry regretted the “public spectacle” she made of the mission, famously kissing the ground after the rocket touched back to Earth.

As well as his rockstar credentials, May earned a PhD in astrophysics from Imperial College London in 2007, three decades after pausing his studies to focus on his music career with Queen.

He recently suggested that Queen could be finished with touring after 50 years, explaining that he wants to spend more time with family and on astrophysics.

News.title: Filipino families keep their loved ones close on All Saints' Day
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Her father may no longer be with her, but Lorita Santos keeps the memories they shared close to her heart.

She was among thousands of Filipinos who flocked to cemeteries across Manila on Sunday to visit the graves of their loved ones, marking All Saints’ Day.

For generations, the tradition known locally as Undas has brought families together to remember and honor their dead. The name derives from the Spanish word “honras,” meaning “honors.”

“Just because they have passed away does not mean we should forget them,” said Santos, who visited the resting places of her father and three other relatives.

Her family marks the occasion by offering flowers and candles. Together, they also pray and share snacks.

The visits are an opportunity to share stories about those who have passed away. Santos fondly remembers how her father would give his children and grandchildren small gifts every payday.

“We will never forget that,” she added.

Santos grew up visiting the graves of her relatives, even outside All Saints’ Day. Now, she is teaching her kids to do the same.

“We pass this on to our children to make sure they are aware of the tradition, so that if something happens to us, they know what to do,” Santos said.

Ancestor veneration became intertwined with Catholicism

Encompassing All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day, Nov. 1 and 2, Undas is rooted in Catholic observances but also incorporates beliefs and customs that predate Spanish colonization.

“There is a very long tradition of ancestor worship in the Philippines,” said Nestor Castro, an anthropology lecturer at the University of the Philippines Diliman.

Long before the Spanish arrived, Filipinos honored ancestral spirits known as anito by offering food and other gifts to the dead. These practices were not tied to a particular date but formed part of a broader tradition of ancestor veneration, Castro explained.

The tradition evolved after the Spanish arrived in 1565 and introduced Catholicism and new religious practices, some of which may have come from Mexico.

The two countries have historical ties dating back to Spanish colonial rule, when the Manila-Acapulco galleon trade connected them for centuries. Today, they also have similar customs for honoring the dead and remembering loved ones.

In Mexico, many families also honor their departed loved ones by spending a day or night at their graves or setting up altars at home. It is a joyful occasion filled with marigolds, music and food.

Similar customs are observed in other countries with strong Catholic traditions, including Bolivia, Poland and Hungary, where families gather to honor their dead with flowers, candles and prayers.

Family gatherings strengthen ties across generations

In Filipino culture, death is not only a time to honor those who have passed away, but also an occasion that brings families together, Castro said.

During funeral wakes, he added, families wait for relatives who live far away to arrive before burying their loved ones. “That’s when family reunions occur. It’s a binding event.”

That sense of togetherness also extends to Undas. Sticky rice cakes are often shared for the occasion, symbolizing the bonds between relatives through their sticky texture.

“These events foster and solidify kinship relationships,” Castro said.

For Mike Mamaril, a 42-year-old school maintenance employee, visiting his parents’ graves is a custom passed down from his grandparents. He said he makes time for the annual visit, even though he rarely gets another opportunity to go.

The gatherings are also a chance to reminisce about his mother and father, including the lighter moments of his childhood.

“We always talk about who among us got scolded the most,” Mamaril said.
