Sports.title: Sheeraz Expects Canelo Payday After Limping Past Zachenhuber
Sports.content:
Hamzah Sheeraz is openly campaigning for an unearned lottery ticket against Canelo Alvarez, and boxing fans are expected to pretend this makes sense.

Fans online already assume Turki Alalshikh will force this matchup. That speaks volumes about the current matchmaking environment. People expect what they think the money wants instead of the fights worth watching. Canelo has genuine options available. A rematch with Terence Crawford makes sense, while Jaron Ennis, Dmitry Bivol, Lester Martinez, or Osleys Iglesias would each offer far more entertainment.

Sheeraz, in contrast, is the ideal safe business fight. He gives the Riyadh Season brass an easy UK marketing angle, brings a recognizable name to British television, and holds zero real threat of upsetting the apple cart. As Simon Zachenhuber showed, Sheeraz is upright, gets uncomfortable when pressed, lacks defensive subtlety, and struggles to impose his height when someone refuses to fold early.

Against Canelo, Sheeraz would stand right in range, get timed coming in, and walk straight into counters without the ringcraft to survive it. Picking him is about protecting the brand and cashing a check, not testing greatness.

“Why not, bro? Why not test myself against the best,” said Sheeraz to DAZN Boxing when asked yesterday why he wants to fight Canelo. “I’m in this game to be the best, and put myself in there with someone with the likes of Canelo. It’s stuff you can dream of. Every day, I wake up, training harder and harder. It’s starting to become more of a reality. So, now it’s like, let me get in there and let me do my thing.”

Sheeraz did himself no favors during his recent majority decision win against Simon Zachenhuber. The German walked through his shots, pressed him constantly, and exposed his discomfort under fire. Nothing in that performance signaled that Sheeraz belongs in the ring with the face of boxing.

His brief title run did not validate him either. Picking up a vacant WBO belt by blowing out Alem Begic in two rounds proved very little. Begic was 39 with a paper record built on obscure opposition. Sheeraz then vacated rather than face Janibek Alimkhanuly, citing low money and an opponent returning from a failed test. He had every right to walk away, but walking away did not prove he is elite.

The refusal to fight Iglesias makes Sheeraz even harder to sell. Canelo openly suggested Hamzah face the dangerous Cuban to earn the shot. Sheeraz rejected the idea, pointing out that Edgar Berlanga and Jaime Munguia never had to pass such an audition. Canelo might have double standards, but whining about Berlanga does not elevate Hamzah’s resume.

Testing yourself against the best is what you do after you run through actual contenders, not after edging Simon Zachenhuber on a majority decision or blasting out Alem Begic.

If Sheeraz genuinely wanted to “test himself against the best” to prepare for Canelo, Osleys Iglesias was standing right there. Canelo offered him the exact blueprint: beat the Cuban southpaw, prove you belong at the elite tier, and bring real credibility to the table.

Saying “It’s stuff you can dream of” gives the game away. It is a dream because it represents the ultimate lottery ticket: a massive purse, global visibility, and zero downside if he loses to an all-time great. Every fringe contender wakes up training hard with that exact dream.

Wanting the biggest purse in the sport is understandable from a business perspective. Pretending that ambition alone makes you a worthy challenger is the part fans are tired of seeing. If everyone who “wakes up dreaming of Canelo” got the call, the sport would be nothing but exhibition paydays. Until Sheeraz takes on a legitimate threat who can punch back, talking about testing himself just sounds like someone angling for a retirement check.

My sources tell me chances are uncomfortably high, easily hovering around 65% to 75% that Canelo fights Hamzah next. Everything coming out of Riyadh points to Hamzah Sheeraz being the preferred target for that spot: Sheeraz sat ringside in Riyadh, gave pre-fight interviews to DAZN building up the matchup, and openly positioned himself as next in line.

That is standard operating procedure when organizers are preparing the public for an announcement. From the promotional side, Sheeraz checks the exact commercial boxes Turki Alalshikh looks for. He provides a British draw to anchor UK pay-per-view buys, brings a Middle Eastern connection based out of Dubai, and comes without the brutal negotiating headaches that accompany figures like Dmitry Bivol or Terence Crawford.

For Canelo, the risk calculus makes Sheeraz almost irresistible. After working through twelve rounds with Christian Mbilli, taking on an upright target who does not use angles or elite lateral footwork is a safe day at the office. Canelo avoids the nightmare styles of Osleys Iglesias or Jaron Ennis while pocketing another massive purse.

The only real hurdles that could derail it are: Crawford agreeing to unretire for the massive bag that a rematch would command. If Crawford says yes, every other fight gets pushed aside immediately. A sudden pivot to a mandatory unification, such as Osleys Iglesias holding the IBF belt or the winner of Janibek Alimkhanuly against Jacob Bank for the vacant WBO strap, if organizers decide they want all the belts consolidated again. Lester Martinez, who holds the WBC interim belt and was also sitting ringside, is being enforced as a mandatory obligation.

As such, unless Crawford signs on the dotted line or public ridicule forces a change in direction, all arrows point toward Sheeraz getting the nod. It is safe matchmaking dressed up as an international event.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Talks Mayweather While His Team Pursues Teofimo
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia says Floyd Mayweather needs to 

“We’ve seen Ryan Garcia say on Twitter that he wants to fight on February 6th, whether it’s against Floyd Mayweather or Teofimo Lopez. I was told that Mayweather wasn’t even in discussion for the next fight,” said Mike Coppinger to DAZN Boxing. “Of course, Mayweather is almost 50 years old now. It’s kind of a pipe dream. It would be a massive event, especially if it was later in the year. First, they’re working on finalizing a fight between Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez, a welterweight title unification. I think it’s one of the biggest fights in all of boxing. Teofimo just regained a title fight in Rolly Romero. I want to see it.”

Teofimo brings plenty of credibility without dragging Mayweather into the promotion. He presents an active, dangerous test with quick hands, explosive pop, elite counter striking. Garcia always carries dynamite in his left hook, though overcommitting against someone as sharp as Lopez creates immediate trouble.

That title bout stands on its own merit. Taking down Lopez proves infinitely more in today’s landscape than defeating an exhibition headliner pushing fifty, regardless of casual fan buzz. As Claudia Trejo noted, Garcia commands attention whenever he speaks. That massive platform works wonders, yet chasing a ghost can drown out the legitimate challenge right in front of him.

Setting a February date proves Garcia wants to compete this winter. It definitely does not prove Mayweather is scrambling to meet a deadline. With Lopez occupying the real negotiating table, Garcia’s final warning sounds like pure noise.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Calls For Terence Crawford Rematch After Win
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez made his priority clear right after taking down Christian Mbilli in Riyadh to grab back the WBC super middleweight strap: he wants another shot at Terence Crawford.

In his post-fight interview, Canelo didn’t hide his intentions when asked about coaxing Crawford out of retirement.

“Hopefully, yes. Hopefully, yes. We would honestly love to have that rematch, like I’ve told you. If not, we’ll keep moving forward with our career, but hopefully that fight can happen,” Canelo said.

The desire is there. The evidence of meaningful improvement is harder to find. Beating Mbilli restores Canelo’s position as a champion, but defeating a pressure fighter does not demonstrate that he would fare better against Crawford’s movement, timing, and ability to control distance.

Whether the Mexican star cares about the potential of losing again is unclear. Assuming Turki is on board with financing a second fight, the money Canelo would get would make it worthwhile.

The appetite from fans for a sequel is lukewarm at best, and for good reason. The first bout settled whatever competitive debate existed. Crawford put on a clinic in ring generalship, using distance, a sharp jab, lateral movement, and timely ties inside to neutralize Canelo. While purists could appreciate Crawford’s discipline, it was a pedestrian viewing experience for the casual paying crowd.

Fans remember twelve rounds of Canelo plodding forward, swinging at air, unable to cut off the ring, while Crawford played keep-away and banked rounds on the outside. Rematches of fights like that rarely produce fireworks; they usually produce a carbon copy.

Boxing fans would far rather see matchups that guarantee genuine action and modern divisional relevance: A unification clash with Osleys Iglesias gives hardcore fans an intriguing, high-risk clash against a dangerous, prime southpaw puncher holding the missing IBF strap.

Even a bout against Dmitry Bivol at light heavyweight would hold more competitive curiosity than watching Crawford stick and move his way to another lopsided decision.

The only real driver behind a Crawford rematch is pure business. Turki Alalshikh has the deep pockets to bankroll a massive spectacle, and both fighters stand to collect generational checks. The promotional build would lean on celebrity hype and pageantry, but inside the ring, the paying audience knows exactly what it would look like: twelve more rounds of perimeter defense and frustration.

Sports.title: Alvarez victorious over Mbilli, captures WBC super middleweight title
Sports.content:
Canelo Álvarez (64-3-2, 39 KOs) reclaimed the WBC super middleweight title with a twelve-round unanimous decision over Christian Mbilli (29-1-1, 24 KOs) on Saturday at Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Canelo’s cleaner counters and defensive work earned him scores of 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110 in the DAZN PPV main event.

Returning from a thirteen-month absence following his loss to Terence Crawford, Álvarez landed in bursts while Mbilli pressed forward without consistently connecting cleanly.

Mbilli had success when he sustained his attacks, but too often backed away after throwing, allowing Álvarez time to choose his counters. Canelo’s jab, hooks and uppercuts supplied the more accurate work, although Mbilli’s activity kept several rounds competitive.

In the eighth, referee Hector Afu deducted a point from Mbilli following an illegal punch. Álvarez had repeatedly drawn the referee’s attention to Mbilli’s fouls before the penalty.

Mbilli continued pressing late but could not produce the breakthrough he needed. Álvarez finished effectively in the final two rounds, securing the decision without either fighter scoring a knockdown.

WBA super middleweight champion Jaime Munguía (47-2, 35 KOs) had a much harder evening than the scorecards suggested against Russian southpaw Nikita Zon (12-1-1, 10 KOs). Munguía retained his title by unanimous decision, winning 116-112 and 117-111 twice after twelve competitive rounds.

Their sixth round produced furious action, with both fighters hurt and Munguía in serious danger before recovering. The Mexican’s combinations and greater output helped him through the later rounds, but Zon remained dangerous until the finish.

Munguía’s defensive lapses made this an uncomfortable first defense against an opponent making his first twelve-round appearance.

Rafael Espinoza (29-0, 25 KOs) retained his WBO featherweight title with a third-round TKO over Ricardo Blandón. The ringside doctor stopped the scheduled twelve-round contest at 1:22 because of a severe cut over Blandón’s eye.

Espinoza controlled the action with his jab and pressure. The medical intervention brought an abrupt ending before the challenger’s corner could attempt further treatment between rounds.

Carl Jammes Martin (29-0, 21 KOs) overcame a seventh-round knockdown to take the WBC Silver featherweight title from David Picasso (33-2-1, 18 KOs) by split decision over ten rounds.

Martin bloodied Picasso’s nose with a left hand in the third. Picasso answered in the seventh with a left hook that dropped the Filipino southpaw, who rose quickly and continued.

Martin’s strong final round helped him secure scores of 95-94 and 96-93, while the third judge favored Picasso 95-94.

Super featherweight Reito Tsutsumi (6-0, 5 KOs) stopped Raymundo Rojas García (16-3, 11 KOs) at 2:27 of the second round. The Japanese southpaw scored two knockdowns in the second before a follow-up attack prompted the referee to stop the scheduled ten-round bout.

Bek Nurmaganbet (17-0, 15 KOs) knocked out Marcos Vázquez Rodríguez (21-4-1, 10 KOs) at 2:57 of the opening round in their scheduled ten-round contest. Nurmaganbet scored an initial knockdown with approximately a minute remaining, then finished the Mexican southpaw with a combination that sent him onto his back.

Brayan León (13-0, 9 KOs) earned an eight-round unanimous decision over Hector Aguirre (7-1, 3 KOs) in a lively super middleweight contest. León landed the heavier punches early, but Aguirre rallied and kept the fight competitive.

Both men landed well in the closing rounds before León received scores of 77-75 and 78-74 twice.

Emiliano Rojo (22-0, 9 KOs) stopped Flavius Biea (24-4, 12 KOs) in the fourth round of their scheduled eight-round bout. Rojo’s pressure and body punching wore down the Romanian veteran, bringing the stoppage midway through the fourth.

Sultan Almohammed (6-0, 4 KOs) defeated Erick Jahir Urvina Villegas (5-3-3, 1 KO) by unanimous decision over six rounds. The eighteen-year-old scored a final-round knockdown with a left hand to the chin and won by scores of 60-54 and 59-55 twice.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Defeats Christian Mbilli by Unanimous Decision to Reclaim WBC Title
Sports.content:
Canelo Álvarez (64-3-2) reclaimed the WBC super middleweight title by making Christian Mbilli miss and punishing his approaches, winning a unanimous decision after twelve rounds on Saturday. Returning from thirteen months out following his defeat to Terence Crawford, Canelo showed that pressure alone was not enough to overwhelm him.

The judges scored it 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110, with Boxing News 24 scoring it 116-111. Mbilli (29-1-1) supplied the greater activity in stretches, but Canelo’s cleaner counters, jab and defensive work gave him the stronger scoring punches across enough rounds to secure the victory.

Canelo established that difference early. Mbilli came forward with energy and tried to force a fast pace, only to find that much of his offense struck the guard or missed. Canelo answered selectively, catching the champion as he entered rather than trying to match every burst with an equally long combination.

The opening three rounds favored Canelo’s accuracy on our card. His jab helped him judge the distance, while his counters discouraged Mbilli from attacking without caution. The champion was working hard, but the effort did not consistently produce clean connections.

Mbilli improved in the fourth, landing more frequently and forcing Canelo into a largely defensive role. That was the approach he needed to sustain: make Canelo respond to several attacks rather than give him time to select a single counter. When Mbilli kept the work coming, the rounds became considerably harder to separate.

The sixth provided another productive spell for the champion. Canelo spent time backing up and near the ropes, answering with occasional body shots and counters while Mbilli supplied the steadier offense. Those passages kept the fight competitive and showed why Canelo could not afford to rely entirely on isolated punches.

Canelo responded in the seventh with one of his better rounds. A stiff jab interrupted Mbilli’s output, and a sharp right uppercut caught him coming forward. Canelo also mixed in body work, giving the champion more to consider before launching his next attack.

The eighth brought a costly point deduction against Mbilli from referee Hector Afu. Canelo’s cleaner work earned him the round on our card, making it 10-8 after the penalty. That gave the challenger additional breathing room without either fighter having scored a knockdown.

Mbilli continued competing rather than allowing the deduction to end his effort. His activity narrowly earned him the ninth and tenth on our card, as Canelo left enough gaps between attacks for the champion to collect points. Canelo remained accurate, but accuracy still needed sufficient output to win those rounds.

The closing two rounds settled matters. Canelo beat Mbilli to openings in the eleventh and finished behind his jab and counters in the twelfth. Mbilli could not generate the sustained late attack needed to threaten a reversal, and Canelo reached the final bell without a serious scare.

This was a successful return built on skills that survived the layoff: timing, punch selection and the ability to defend while remaining close enough to answer. Mbilli made him work and earned rounds through persistence, but never consistently solved the difference between getting Canelo to the ropes and landing effectively once he had him there.

Canelo did not deliver a stoppage, extending his run of distance fights, but he earned the belt with the more precise boxing. Mbilli brought the pressure expected of him; Canelo repeatedly supplied the better answer.

Sports.title: Canelo vs Mbilli Live Results: Round-by-Round Updates and DAZN Coverage
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía (47-2, 35 KOs) retained his WBA super middleweight title with a unanimous decision over Nikita Zon (12-1-1, 10 KOs), but looked alarmingly poor in a fight closer than the scores suggested. The judges returned cards of 117-111, 116-112 and 117-111, margins that flattered the champion after a difficult twelve rounds.

Zon repeatedly found openings for his southpaw power shots, exposing Munguía’s loose defense and hurting him badly during a furious sixth round. Munguía survived that crisis and answered with volume and combinations, but never produced the commanding performance expected against such an inexperienced challenger.

The referee also appeared to miss two potential knockdowns against Munguía, allowing him to escape counts that could have materially affected the scoring. A clear rabbit punch from Munguía went without a point deduction, another officiating failure that favored the champion. Munguía left with the belt, but his defensive mistakes and reliance on outworking Zon made this an unsettling defense rather than a reassuring victory.

Featherweight champion Rafael Espinoza (29-0, 25 KOs) retained his WBO title with a third-round TKO over Ricardo Blandón (21-7, 14 KOs) after a severe cut over the challenger’s eye forced a medical stoppage.

Espinoza controlled the early action with his jab and reach, keeping Blandón under pressure. The Nicaraguan struggled to get past the champion’s long punches and establish an attack of his own. The cut worsened enough for the ringside doctor to intervene, ending the scheduled twelve-round contest.

Blandón had accepted the fight on roughly a week’s notice after Lorenzo Parra was ruled out, and the gap in preparation accompanied a substantial difference in class. Espinoza was comfortably in charge, although the medical ending denied him the chance to produce a more decisive finish with his punches. It was a straightforward retention for the champion, but a brief and unsatisfying title fight against a replacement challenger.

Super featherweight Reito Tsutsumi (6-0, 5 KOs) overwhelmed Raymundo Rojas García (16-3, 11 KOs) for a second-round TKO in their scheduled ten-round bout. The Japanese southpaw took charge early, using his speed to land clean combinations before Rojas could establish himself.

Rojas struggled to cope with the quicker, more polished prospect and could not slow his attack. Tsutsumi kept pressing, turning his technical advantage into damaging offense rather than allowing the Mexican time to recover.

The second-round stoppage completed a one-sided performance and gave Tsutsumi his fifth consecutive knockout victory. Rojas brought regional experience and respectable punching power, but neither was enough to bridge the difference in speed and technique. Tsutsumi looked ready for a sterner test after another opponent failed to take him beyond the early rounds.

Carl Jammes Martin (29-0) upset David Picasso (33-2-1, 18 KOs) by split decision over ten rounds to claim the WBC Silver featherweight title. The Filipino southpaw started quickly, using his speed and cleaner power shots to prevent the taller favorite from settling.

Picasso had substantial height and reach advantages but too often allowed Martin to dictate the pace rather than keeping him outside. Martin’s busier work and heavier-looking punches gave him the stronger argument in rounds where neither fighter sustained control.

Picasso had his successes in a competitive fight, but his quieter stretches left openings for Martin to seize the initiative. Two judges favored the unbeaten challenger, rewarding a performance built on activity and effective aggression against a more established opponent. Moving up in weight, Martin earned a significant victory while Picasso paid for failing to make his physical advantages count.

Super featherweight Sultan Almohammed (6-0) scored a sixth-round knockdown on his way to a unanimous decision over Erick Jahir Urvina Villegas after six rounds. The 18-year-old Saudi prospect dictated the action with persistent pressure, making the Mexican fight at his pace.

Almohammed maintained his intensity throughout, but Urvina Villegas proved tougher to finish than some of the teenager’s earlier opponents. The Mexican kept battling despite being outworked, forcing the heavy favorite to go the distance.

Almohammed closed strongly, putting Urvina Villegas down in the final round to underline his superiority. The knockdown capped a clear victory, even if the prospect could not produce another early stoppage. Six rounds against an opponent who kept competing gave Almohammed useful work beyond the quick finishes that had marked his early career.

Super middleweight Bek Nurmaganbet (17-0, 15 KOs) demolished Marcos Vázquez Rodríguez (21-4-1, 10 KOs) with a first-round knockout, ending their scheduled ten-round fight at 2:57. The unbeaten Kazakh attacked early with heavy, accurate punches, giving the Mexican veteran little opportunity to settle.

Nurmaganbet scored two knockdowns as his southpaw power proved too much for the 37-year-old. The violent finish immediately drew Knockout of the Year talk from DAZN.

Vázquez Rodríguez’s experience offered little protection once Nurmaganbet began landing, and he was overwhelmed before the opening round was over. This was a destructive performance, although beating an older opponent coming off a defeat leaves tougher tests ahead. Nurmaganbet supplied the kind of emphatic finish expected from a heavy favorite and delivered one of the early undercard’s biggest moments.

Emiliano Rojo stopped Flavius Biea at 1:37 of the fourth round, securing Team Mexico’s first victory of the night in their super middleweight bout. The 20-year-old controlled the middleweight bout with steady pressure, walking down his Romanian opponent and making him work at Rojo’s pace. Biea (24-4, 12 KOs) struggled to halt the younger fighter’s advance as Rojo’s activity gradually wore him down.

Rojo (22-0, 9 KOs) looked comfortable taking the initiative against the more experienced veteran, keeping the pressure on until the referee intervened. It was an effective performance, although Biea’s recent stoppage defeats limit how much can be read into the result. The 20-year-old Rojo did what a heavy favorite needed to do, finishing an opponent whose career was already heading downhill.

Super middleweight prospect Brayan León (13-0, 9 KOs) defeated Hector Aguirre by an eight-round unanimous decision, but the unbeaten Cuban had to work for it. Aguirre pressed León and forced him into a tough, competitive fight that exposed some flaws in the favored prospect.

León started rounds well, only to let his work rate drop and allow Aguirre to back him up. Those lapses gave the Mexican opportunities to keep the action close rather than letting León take control.

Aguirre lacked the punching power to make those stretches more costly, but he pushed León through the full eight rounds before suffering his first professional defeat.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Survives Sixth Round Scare to Outpoint Nikita Zon
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía (47-2, 35 KOs) retained his WBA super middleweight title against Nikita Zon (12-1-1, 10 KOs), but his dreadful defense and a dangerous sixth round made the unanimous decision far less comfortable than the scorecards suggested. The champion won by scores of 117-111, 116-112 and 117-111 after twelve rounds that exposed how easily he can still be hurt.

Zon arrived with limited experience and no previous twelve-round fights, yet repeatedly found Munguía with effective southpaw power shots. The Mexican’s volume and combinations helped him collect rounds, but they did not conceal the damage coming back. This was supposed to be a favorable title defense; instead, Munguía spent portions of it fighting to keep the challenger from taking over.

The sixth round brought the clearest danger. Zon hurt Munguía badly and pressed an attack that threatened to turn a difficult evening into another stoppage defeat. Munguía deserves credit for surviving and responding, but the crisis came against an opponent taking an enormous jump in competition.

His recovery mattered. Munguía resumed throwing combinations and used his activity to rebuild his case over the later rounds. Zon could land the more troubling punches without consistently matching the champion’s output, giving Munguía a route to winning rounds even when his defensive mistakes were the most memorable feature.

That distinction helps explain the decision without making the wide margins persuasive. Munguía’s busy spells counted, but Zon’s successes were too significant for this to resemble a routine defense. The challenger was dangerous enough to punish openings that Munguía should have been closing well before the championship rounds.

The officiating also deserved scrutiny. Two sequences in which Munguía appeared to go down were not ruled knockdowns, allowing him to avoid counts and the potential scoring consequences. Those were important moments in a contest where the official margins already seemed generous to the champion.

Munguía also escaped a point deduction for a clear rabbit punch. That foul warranted stronger action, particularly in a physical fight where the challenger was already having to overcome a substantial experience disadvantage. Taken together, the missed potential knockdowns and unpunished foul made the referee’s performance part of the story.

Zon did not need to win every round to expose the shortcomings in Munguía’s work. He found opportunities to land hard while the champion was attacking, showing the cost of throwing combinations without adequately protecting the return. Munguía could produce more punches and still emerge from a sequence looking like the more vulnerable fighter.

The concern carries added weight because Munguía has already suffered a knockout loss to Bruno Surace. Surviving Zon’s best attack prevented a repeat result, but it did not demonstrate that the underlying defensive weaknesses have been corrected. An inexperienced challenger was still able to bring him close to disaster.

For Zon, the defeat supplied evidence that his power could trouble a world champion over a distance he had never previously attempted. He fell short on the cards, but made a much stronger case for himself than the pre-fight expectations suggested.

Munguía kept his belt through persistence, offensive volume and the ability to recover when badly hurt. Those qualities earned him something on a poor night, but they cannot keep substituting for reliable defense. Against a more accomplished finisher, the openings Zon found could carry a much heavier price.

Sports.title: Rafael Espinoza Stops Ricardo Blandon on Cuts in Riyadh Under Three Rounds
Sports.content:
Rafael Espinoza (29-0, 25 KOs) retained his WBO featherweight title with a third-round TKO over Ricardo Blandón (21-7, 14 KOs), but a severe cut ended the fight before it could become much of a contest. The champion was comfortably ahead when the ringside doctor intervened on Saturday’s Canelo Alvarez–Christian Mbilli undercard in Riyadh.

Blandón accepted the opportunity on roughly a week’s notice after mandatory challenger Lorenzo Parra was ruled out. He faced a difficult task against Espinoza, and the opening rounds offered little indication that he could overcome the difference in technique. The Mexican established his jab, applied pressure, and made the replacement challenger work to get within punching distance.

Espinoza’s length gave him control of the approach. Blandón needed to get past the jab before he could make his own power useful, but he struggled to do that consistently. The champion could initiate the action from farther out, leaving the Nicaraguan trying to close ground while dealing with incoming punches.

That combination of reach and pressure made Espinoza difficult to dislodge. He did not have to surrender the initiative to use his physical advantages, and Blandón never established enough offense to make him reconsider his approach. For the brief time they fought, the champion dictated the terms.

The cut became the decisive factor in the third round. Its severity prompted the doctor to stop the contest, producing a TKO rather than allowing the scheduled twelve-round bout to continue. This was a medical ending, with the condition of Blandón’s eye determining the finish rather than a knockdown or a referee intervention during an unanswered attack.

That distinction matters when judging the performance. Espinoza was winning clearly, but the fight ended before he could demonstrate how thoroughly he might break down the challenger. The result rewarded his early control without providing the more complete finish that his pressure appeared capable of producing.

For Blandón, the short preparation and sudden ending made this a frustrating world-title opportunity. He arrived with four consecutive victories and respectable punching power, but neither translated into sustained success against the champion. Once the cut became too serious, there was no opportunity to attempt a recovery over the remaining rounds.

Espinoza had been out of action since stopping Arnold Khegai in November 2025. Returning with a successful defense keeps his championship run moving, although fewer than three completed rounds offered limited work after that absence. Blandón could not extend him enough to reveal much about his longer-distance sharpness.

The original opponent change also reduced what Espinoza could gain from the night. Beating a replacement challenger was necessary to protect his position, but it was unlikely to carry the significance of a successful mandatory defense against Parra. The abrupt medical stoppage narrowed that opportunity further.

Espinoza remains a difficult proposition at featherweight because his unusual height comes with an attacking style that prevents opponents from simply waiting outside. Blandón experienced that difficulty immediately. The champion kept his belt with little trouble, but a stronger opponent and a fuller contest are needed to give his next defense greater substance.

Having a world champion like Espinoza share the ring with a replacement drafted on seven days notice made for grim viewing. You could tell within ninety seconds Blandon had neither the footwork nor the size to deal with a six foot one featherweight, let alone mount meaningful offense.

Blandon was essentially a sacrifice brought in to salvage television time once Lorenzo Parra fell out. When the doctor stepped in to halt it over that eye cut, it almost felt like an act of mercy rather than a dramatic championship conclusion. Nobody gained anything from it. Espinoza gets a three round workout that told us nothing new, Blandon collects a paycheck after taking punishment, and the audience gets robbed of a genuine title contest.

Ghana News.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
Ghana News.content:
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday.

The remaining 10% may take longer to source in the required amounts, the company added.

Binance has consistently pledged to cover 100% of the losses from what is suspected to be crypto's biggest hack on record and said it has set aside more than $6.34bn in company funds to do so.

"Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on Saturday.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the hack.

Two analytics firms previously told the BBC they had robust intelligence pointing to North Korean state-backed hacking unit the Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor - which was specifically named by the FBI - as the likely culprits.

Binance said it had replenished the stolen assets using various funds and its own corporate treasury.

All holdings of the cryptocurrencies bitcoin, ethereum and Tether are covered, along with seven other widely-traded crypto assets, the company said.

The company said its next goal is resuming withdrawal services for users, saying it remained on track to reopen withdrawals on Sunday 1 November and would provide a further update once details were confirmed.

The hack is believed to be the largest in history, eclipsing the record of a $1.5bn heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025 - for which the FBI also said North Korea was responsible.

North Korea has always denied involvement in these attacks.

Binance's initial investigation suggested an engineer's laptop was compromised, which allowed access to unauthorised withdrawals, but a later update said they had uncovered "additional points of breach".

Richard Teng, Binance's co-chief executive officer, said the hack was carried out by more than one person, and the hackers used sophisticated methods to hide their tracks, such as a "self-destruct mechanism".

On Friday, the company said it had frozen around $3bn of stolen assets after working with law enforcement, intelligence firms and partners.

The investigation is ongoing, it added. The US Secret Service said on Friday it is "working around the clock" with private sector partners "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds" stolen from Binance.

Binance, founded in China in 2017, lets users buy, sell and trade digital assets - it is estimated to have hundreds of millions of users worldwide.

Crypto is a digital asset, which doesn't exist physically and is instead accessed via digital wallets or computers.

Ghana News.title: Unreligious Servants marks fourth anniversary with charity donation to Chosen Rehabilitation Centre
Ghana News.content:
The creative group Unreligious Servants has marked its fourth anniversary with the official launch of its debut album, First Service, alongside a charitable donation to the Chosen Rehabilitation Centre.

The group’s Deputy Director, Kwesi Brenya Baah, said the initiative forms part of its commitment to using creative talents to spread the Christian message and contribute to society.

Speaking during the anniversary celebration on Saturday, October 31, he explained that Unreligious Servants was established four years ago by individuals from different creative fields, including music, photography and design, who shared a common desire to give back to society.

He said members had committed their creative works and intellectual property rights to the group, ensuring that all proceeds generated from its projects, including the newly launched album, would go entirely towards charitable activities.

Mr Brenya Baah explained that the name Unreligious Servants was inspired by the desire to distinguish the group through its actions rather than religious labels.

He stressed that the group was not anti-religious but was made up of Christians seeking to demonstrate their faith through service, compassion and practical contributions to society.

As part of the anniversary activities, the group returned to Chosen Rehabilitation Centre, which was the first institution it supported when it began its charitable work, to worship and interact with residents and donate essential supplies.

The items presented included bags of rice, beans, gari, cooking oil, palm oil, spaghetti and tissue paper, among other provisions, to support the centre's upkeep.

According to him, the group's previous visit had inspired members to do more after witnessing the impact of their intervention, prompting them to return on the occasion of their fourth anniversary.

He commended Chosen for its rehabilitation efforts, particularly its faith-based approach, which combines the teachings of the Bible with practical support to help individuals overcome their challenges and rebuild their lives.

He noted that the centre also provides skills-development opportunities and facilities, including a recording studio and a computer laboratory, to equip residents with relevant skills and improve their chances of reintegrating into society.

Mr Brenya Baah appealed to individuals and organisations to support the centre, which he said accommodates approximately 120 to 130 people and is doing important work in rehabilitating vulnerable individuals.

He said the group's anniversary celebration was not only an opportunity to reflect on its four-year journey but also to renew its commitment to using creativity, faith and collective action to make a meaningful difference in society.

Ghana News.title: 8 dead, 21 rescued in bus collision on Elubo–Takoradi Highway
Ghana News.content:
Eight people have died following a fatal collision between an Ivorian passenger bus and a parked Burkinabè bus at Azuletti, near Samenye, along the Elubo–Takoradi Highway.

The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) said its Elubo station rescued 21 passengers following the crash, which occurred on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at about 7:26 p.m.

According to the Service in a post shared on Facebook, the Ivorian-registered bus, with registration number AB-415-AN, was travelling towards Benin when it rammed into the rear of a stationary Burkinabè passenger bus, registered KJA-5604J.

The parked vehicle was reportedly obstructing one lane of the highway, resulting in the collision.

Seven people were pronounced dead at the scene, while another victim later died at the hospital, bringing the death toll to eight.

The 21 rescued passengers, who sustained injuries, were transported to the nearest hospital for medical attention.

The bodies of the deceased were subsequently handed over to the police.

Preliminary investigations suggest that speeding may have contributed to the crash, although further investigations are expected to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incident.

Ghana News.title: Over 100 wooden structures destroyed in Taifa fire, ECG transformer gutted at Lapaz
Ghana News.content:
More than 100 wooden structures and three metal containers have been destroyed in a commercial fire outbreak at Taifa June-July in the Greater Accra Region.

The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) said firefighters from the Madina Fire Station, supported by personnel from the Headquarters Sub-Station, responded to the incident and battled the blaze.

The fire destroyed more than 100 wooden structures, including their contents, as well as three metal containers.

However, firefighters successfully prevented the fire from spreading to more than 200 adjoining wooden structures and the Sabbath Faith Salvation Church building, which were salvaged.

In a separate incident at Lapaz Tabora No. 5, firefighters from the Dansoman Fire Station responded to an electrical fire involving an Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) transformer.

The transformer was completely destroyed by the fire.

The GNFS confirmed that no casualties or injuries were recorded in either incident.

The Service has urged the public to observe fire safety precautions and promptly report outbreaks to the nearest fire station to facilitate swift emergency response and minimise damage to property and loss of lives.

Ghana News.title: Judge dismisses Trump’s lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein birthday book
Ghana News.content:
A US judge has thrown out President Donald Trump's $10bn dollar lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal, ruling the suit was "grasping at straws".

Trump had sued the media outlet's parent company Dow Jones and its leader Rupert Murdoch last year after it reported on a letter allegedly written by Trump to disgraced financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein as part of a birthday book in 2003, before Epstein was charged with sex crimes.

Trump has denied writing or signing the letter, which included suggestive language and a drawing of the outline of a woman's body.

Judge Darrin Gayles threw out the case, finding the suit runs counter to the First Amendment, which protects freedom of the press.

Gayles had already once dismissed the defamation lawsuit, which sought $20 billion in damages. Trump's team refiled the suit seeking $10 billion, and this time, the judge threw out the case "with prejudice," meaning the suit cannot be filed again.

The news outlet's story about Epstein's 50th birthday book - and the letter with Trump's name - came as the Trump administration battled intense bipartisan criticism over the summer for its handling of Epstein documents.

Trump had said the newspaper had slandered him and violated libel laws in publishing the article.

In his 20-page ruling, Gayles noted the paper's "thoughtful and detailed ​investigation" that led to the story and said the lawsuit was "grasping at ‌straws" to "to manufacture flaws" their work.

The judge wrote that Trump's legal team did not prove that the defendants made defamatory statements with "actual malice", which the law requires be proven.

Actual malice is high bar to meet, as it requires proof that the defendant knew the defamatory statement was false or acted with reckless disregard for whether it was true or not.

Trump alleged that the letter obtained and released by the Journal, which features his signature at the bottom, was "fake" and that the defendants devised the story in order to defame him.

Trump's legal team had argued that because Trump denied writing the letter when contacted by the Journal, the paper should have "disregarded everything else they learned in their investigation and not published the story", Gayles wrote.

"But that is not what the actual malice standard requires and runs afoul of the First Amendment," Gayles wrote.

If that were the law, he wrote, then "any time a public figure or his team denies an accusation, journalists would be immediately blocked from publishing negative or contradictory press—a result that flies in the face of the 'American privilege to speak one's mind'".

According to the Wall Street Journal story, a letter bearing Trump's name "contained several lines of typewritten text framed by the outline of a naked woman, which appears to be hand-drawn with a heavy marker".

It reportedly contained a joking reference that "enigmas never age" and allegedly ended with the words: "A pal is a wonderful thing. Happy Birthday - and may every day be another wonderful secret".

Ghana News.title: Shops looted as German cost of living protests turn violent
Ghana News.content:
Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday and clashes erupted with police there and in other German cities after largely peaceful mass protests over the cost of living.

Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters who targeted emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles.

Thousands earlier joined the demonstrations organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service.

The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday.

A large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off by police, AFP news agency reported. A police spokesperson said many arrests were made in the city.

Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half of what the organisers had estimated on their website. German media say tens of thousands protested in German cities on Saturday.

Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were "to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion".

She said: "What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden."

While protests during the day were largely peaceful, the demonstrations turned violent as night fell.

In a post on X, Frankfurt police said that "violent riots" were occurring in the city centre. The windows of several shops had been smashed and molotov cocktails were thrown at emergency services, police said.

In later updates, officials said the windows of a gun shop were smashed and that they had seized two weapons after arresting a suspect.

Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, of which Frankfurt is the biggest city, said that "around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists" had infiltrated the protest in the city. He added that it was "shameful" how the protests had ended.

Poseck said: "We all have those images from France in our minds – looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers... France must not be held up as a model in this regard."

Ghana News.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials
Ghana News.content:
A federal judge has ordered the federal government to stop threatening local and state election officials with criminal charges over their role in processing election ballots.

The California judge ruled that the Department of Justice (DoJ) must stop demanding that local and state election officials set aside or not process certain ballots that the Trump administration alleges may come from non-citizens.

The ruling comes days before the midterm elections, which will determine which political party controls the US Congress for the last two years of Donald Trump's presidency.

Trump criticised the ruling on Saturday, writing,"Why would they reject fixing Election Fraud?"

In California earlier this month, the justice department sent letters to the secretary of state and Los Angeles County Registrar demanding they set aside the ballots of 20,000 registered voters whom the Trump administration "believe" are "likely" non-citizens, according to court documents.

About a week later, armed officials from the Department of Homeland Security delivered letters to county officials and employees across California threatening criminal charges if they didn't sequester those ballots.

But the groups said they could not comply with those demands because they must follow election procedures required by state and federal law. A judge weighed in and tossed the demand, writing it would "wreak havoc" in the election.

Around the same time, the justice department reportedly began a criminal investigation into county election officials, issuing federal grand jury subpoenas.

Civil rights groups and unions representing election workers filed a legal complaint, accusing the justice department of interfering in their duty to administer the election. Judge Trina Thompson ordered the administration to halt their actions.

"Although Defendants claim that their actions are designed to halt unlawful voting by noncitizens, their actions are likely to have the effect of interfering with election administration and disenfranchising lawful voters," Judge Thompson wrote.

The Trump administration sent a similar letter about alleged non-citizen voters to Washington state and demanded that the secretary of state there cease processing the ballots, according to Thompson's order.

The manoeuvres are part of a yearslong campaign by Trump and his administration to fight alleged voter fraud that they believe is widespread, despite research showing that it is extremely rare.

Ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November, the president has cast doubt on the security of the vote - alleging "rampant" cheating in postal voting and non-citizens voting. The president also offered a $1m (£750,000) reward to people who report cases of voter fraud in the US which lead to a conviction.

Studies, however, suggest actual cases are extremely rare. BBC Verify reported that the Heritage Foundation's database identified 24 cases of non-citizens being convicted for voting between 2005 and 2025.

In his post on Saturday, Trump said criticised recent rulings against his administration pertaining to allegations of possible election fraud and vowed to continue fighting for "Election Integrity".

Ghana News.title: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
Ghana News.content:
There were raw emotional scenes as people evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky crossed from Belarus into the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv.

Families cried as they reunited with relatives they had not seen for years, with two sisters running and crying out as they embraced their father.

Some elderly residents were so weak they were carried on stretchers. They had been trapped in the frontline city without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky thanked US First Lady Melania Trump for her efforts in brokering a local ceasefire that paved the way for their evacuation on Friday.

Upon their arrival, Dasha and Anya Palii sprinted across the tarmac screaming towards the bus carrying their father Mykhailo.

Their cries and their tears captured the sheer relief of three years of desperate worry, fearing they would never see him again.

Their mother Zhanna clasped Mykhailo's face and stroked his forehead again and again, as if checking he was the same man she had left behind. He promised her, finally, they will now get married.

Tetiana and Volodymyr, an older couple carrying their cat, told the BBC they no longer have a home, after it was burned down in the first year of the war. They have been living in the abandoned house of a neighbour.

They said they instantly took the decision to leave but feared their journey could be disrupted. Now they have to work out where to go next and how to rebuild their lives.

Ukrainian military positions lie just 5km (3.1 miles) from Oleshky, but evacuees first had to travel through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, where they flew to Belarus, before finally being driven across Ukraine's northern border on Saturday.

The oldest evacuee was 94 years old, while the youngest was one, according to Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman.

Zelensky said in a post on X that "all of them will receive the assistance they need. It is important that government agencies and all the regional and local authorities involved work effectively and help our people adapt."

Many people bear the scars: the convoy includes as many ambulances as coaches. The impact of years caught between the frontlines is written on the weary faces of many of Oleshky's residents, some hobbling on crutches, others needing wheelchairs.

They have a lot to come to terms with, not least having left the place they call home.

A humanitarian ceasefire took effect across the frontline region of Kherson on Tuesday, providing the first few days of peace in the area in four years, following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Before the war, Oleshky was home to 24,000 people.

Conditions had become so desperate in the city that not only was getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escape was highly dangerous because the routes out had been mined and subject to drone attack.

Bridges across the nearby River Dnipro have been destroyed and sources say the riverbank has been mined and is dangerous.

One resident who fled the city three weeks earlier told the BBC he had walked through 24km (15 miles) of minefields to get to safety.

The ceasefire allowed the road out of the city to be cleared of mines and humanitarian aid to be delivered.

Ceasefire measures will remain in place until the end of Sunday 1 November.

Residents had a four-hour window to leave before a convoy of 25 buses, with space for 750 people, left the town on Friday afternoon - along with ambulances for people with limited mobility.

Several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay in the war-torn city, despite widespread devastation and the lack of gas, electricity and running water.

Some of the older generation did not want to leave, one relative told the BBC.

Lubinets said on Friday morning that those who decided to stay "will receive all the necessary humanitarian assistance".

He and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova travelled to Oleshky together on Friday, setting off from Armiansk, in the Russian-occupied Crimean peninsula.

Lubinets is the first Ukrainian official since the start of the war to visit Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine.

Zelensky praised him and his team for helping move evacuees out to safety.

The Ukrainian president also thanked those who had helped bring attention to the "true humanitarian catastrophe in Ukrainian territory temporarily occupied by Russia".

The ceasefire has required close cooperation between Lubinets and Lantratova, which Lubinets said he carried out in the interests of saving lives.

But some in Ukraine have recoiled at the sight of him standing beside a representative of the Russian occupying power which has killed so many of the city's residents and made life unbearable for the rest.

Russia said on Thursday that it had prepared "dozens of tonnes" of aid for the residents who do not wish to leave, including food, medicine, hygiene products and fuel for generators.

Despite the ceasefire in Oleshky, the war has continued.

Zelensky said that Russia had attacked Ukrainian energy infrastructure, hitting electricity substations, thermal power plants and gas infrastructure.

Ukraine's military said it hit a major Russian producer of missile fuel in the Rostov region.

Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US are due to resume ceasefire talks in Abu Dhabi in early November after discussions were suspended earlier this year due to the Iran war.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
