World.title: Malawi: Police Confirm Egyptian Deputy Ambassador Beaten in Lilongwe Attack
World.content:
A senior Egyptian diplomat has been hospitalised after being attacked and beaten in Lilongwe, sparking a police investigation into the shocking assault.

National Police spokesperson Gladys Chiwaula confirmed that Egypt's Deputy Ambassador to Malawi was admitted to a hospital in the capital after the attack.

"Police are following up on the matter and will give more details later," she said.

Chiwaula gave few details.

She did not say where the attack happened, what led to it, or how serious the diplomat's injuries are. Police have also withheld the deputy ambassador's name.

Officers say they are investigating, but the incident is likely to raise alarm over the safety of foreign envoys in the country.

World.title: Africa: From Commonwealth Connections to Economic Opportunity - Expanding Africa-Caribbean Trade Linkages
World.content:
guest column

When Commonwealth leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda this November, they will confront rising trade tensions, geopolitical shocks and supply chain disruption alongside longstanding challenges, such as high debt, limited affordable finance, climate exposure and poor connectivity.

Across Africa, the Pacific and the Caribbean, these pressures make diversifying markets, attracting productive investment and building resilience through trade even more urgent. They also increase the importance of regional and cross-regional value chains that can withstand disruptions to established trade relationships.

One opportunity lies in plain sight: stronger Africa-Caribbean economic connections. Shared history, culture and diaspora relationships provide a foundation, as do common ambitions to diversify exports, add value locally and create opportunities for small businesses, including those led by women and young entrepreneurs.

The institutional landscape is also changing. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is building a framework for trade including goods, services, investment and digital commerce, while the Caribbean is deepening the CARICOM Single Market and Economy.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Connecting these integration efforts across the Atlantic could help firms aggregate supply and demand, build scale, and develop regional value chains. and access larger markets. A bigger, more integrated market can improve the commercial case for investment and the economics of cross-regional trade.

Forthcoming analysis by the International Trade Centre (ITC), undertaken with the support of Afreximbank, points to considerable unrealised trade potential between Africa and the Caribbean. But the numbers tell only part of the story.

In a survey of 1,175 businesses and business support organisations only 10% of African companies and 12% of Caribbean companies reported trading with the other region. Yet among those that did, 79% of African firms and 82% of Caribbean firms described their experience positively or very positively. The challenge is less about potential than removing barriers to scale.

Businesses struggle to access reliable market information, trusted partners and appropriate finance, as well as to navigate standards and move goods efficiently.

These constraints are not new. Low trade volumes weaken direct transport links; poor connectivity raises costs; limited commercial relationships restrict information; and smaller transactions are harder to finance.

The priority is to tackle these challenges in a comprehensive way.

Physical distance remains particularly costly. ITC estimates freight costs on African exports to the Caribbean at almost 20% of shipment value, compared with just over 8% for African exports globally. Caribbean exports to Africa face costs approaching 22%. Limited routes and fragmented networks continue to undermine viable trade. Scheduled direct air services between Lagos and Barbados, launched in 2026, illustrate how improved connections can support business travel, tourism and wider services.

Access to finance depends not only on the availability of capital, but on whether viable opportunities can be connected to appropriate financing. Businesses need guidance on available funding and lender requirements, and financial institutions need appropriate instruments and ways to manage risk. Trade finance, working-capital facilities, guarantees and risk-sharing mechanisms can all bridge these gaps.

Payments also matter, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Slow, costly or uncertain transfers can derail transactions. More efficient cross-border payment systems would reduce both transaction costs and risks. Africa's Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) offers useful lessons for simplifying payments as financial links with the Caribbean deepen.

Beyond trade volumes, value creation extends beyond goods. Services, digital solutions and the creative industries can generate more value within both regions. Africa and the Caribbean have globally recognised cultural assets and extensive diasporas, yet much of the creative value is captured elsewhere. Creators and firms need finance, workable payments, intellectual property expertise, distribution channels and direct access to buyers and investors. Supporting creative businesses, rather than only promoting cultural exchange, would generate more revenue and help jobs remain in local economies.

Governments and institutions can create the enabling environment, but businesses will ultimately determine whether a new chapter in Africa–Caribbean economic relations succeed, especially for SMEs.

Commonwealth trade and investment platforms can connect policymakers, investors, entrepreneurs and business leaders. They offer a way to identify obstacles that no single firm or government can resolve alone. Success, however, means introductions becoming contracts, investment reaching viable enterprises and businesses entering new markets.

The Commonwealth brings an existing economic advantage to this endeavour. The opportunity is to make that advantage work more deliberately for Africa–Caribbean commerce, where physical distance, limited market information and still-thin commercial networks continue to constrain trade.

Through its Working Group on Trade and Investment, member countries are developing a workplan to expand intra-Commonwealth commerce. Cooperation on compatible regulations, mutual recognition of standards and qualifications, and simpler border procedures can help realise these gains.

Close 

ITC's work on investment promotion and digital trade to women's economic empowerment, small-state resilience and emerging Africa–Caribbean business linkages can advance this agenda. Afreximbank's Global Africa vision brings the finance, investment and commercial infrastructure required to turn diaspora ties into sustainable economic relationships.

These capabilities are complementary. Trade policy can open markets; finance helps businesses act; and enterprises sustain commercial relationships.

The practical test is clear: identify viable opportunities, mobilise investment, resolve logistics, finance and payment barriers, connect SMEs to customers and investors, use digital trade to overcome distance and retain more value within regions. Progress should then be measured in transactions, market access and sustainable business relationships.

As leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda, they can demonstrate how a connected Commonwealth can convert partnerships into investment, enterprise and shared prosperity.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Kill Police Inspector, 11 Others in Kebbi
World.content:
Residents of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi in Besse/Shanga riverine areas of Kebbi State have fled their communities as suspected members of the Lakurawa and Mamudawa terror groups killed 11 residents and a police inspector in a series of attacks they have launched on the communities.

The terrorists carried out a series of attacks on the communities in Besse and Shanga from the 22nd to 28 October, this year, Daily Trust gathered. During the attacks, they burnt houses and looted property as they moved along the River Niger bank from Kaoje to Besse.

A local who spoke to our corespondent, Aminu Usman, said the attack on the communities was devastating as the gunmen burnt houses and property before retreating to their hideouts.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said, "the attack took many of the villagers unawares. No one expected that the Lakurawa terrorists would attack us. The attack was carried out in a coordinated manner. They burnt our houses and looted our property. Many people have been rendered homeless and they have fled the communities," he said.

Though the police said five people were killed in an attack on October 26, while seven others died in attacks on October 28 in the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi area of the state, bringing the total to 12, including a police inspector, locals who spoke under condition of anonymity said over 23 people actually lost their lives in the Lakurawa/Mamudawa attacks on the communities of Koko Besse and Shanga areas of Kebbi.

A source said, "They killed people and took their valuables. They burnt motorcycles and broke into shops and took whatever they wanted."

He added that rumour of the attacks triggered the mobilisation of vigilantes known as Yan Sakai, who allegedly attacked some Fulani traders at Samanaji Market on October 22, 2026.

A resident who spoke to our correspondent said, "I know a man who lost four of his family members in the attack. As I speak, only a few people are left in the affected communities. Some of them who fled for safety during the attack are just returning on the assurance by the security agents and government that measures are being put in place to ensure our safety."

He called on the government to come to their aid as some of the residents have nowhere to stay.

Another resident, Aliyu Tailor Besse, said the attack was carried out by the Lakurawa terrorists group.

"What happened was that after attacking communities in Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government, they started moving along the River Niger up to Koko Besse area.They were attacking communities along the River Niger as they moved towards Besse community. Many people were killed in the attacks. Prior to the attacks, those who saw them moving along the River Niger banks had raised an alarm calling on residents of the communities along the area to vacate. Some left, but many others stayed behind," he said.

Daily Trust gathered that a few days before the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi attacks, suspected members of the Lakurawa group also attacked Lafagu and other communities in Boya area of Kaoje, killing the village head, Alhaji Saidu Mujeli, and six others before leaving the area through the River Niger bank to attack other communities in Besse and Shanga.

It was gathered that despite the establishment of an army battalion in Kaoje to curtail the activities of terrorists, attacks have continued.

Police confirm attacks

Speaking to our correspondent, the state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, said "it's true that the attack happened but it did not happen in one day and not in one community. It started from the 22nd of this month. The casualties recorded was not in a single attack. They attacked many of the communities in the riverine area and that's why the figure of those killed rose to 12. A police inspector and 11 others were killed in the attacks."

He said members of the Lakurawa terrorists group had earlier attacked communities along the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi axis on 22nd of October, but security operatives repelled them. He said they later carried out attacks on the communities of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi on October 26 and 28.

"Although the joint security teams repelled the attacks, seven people unfortunately lost their lives, including a police inspector," he said.

He added that earlier, members of the Yan Sakai, had invaded Samanaji Market and killed Fulani traders.

"Our police tactical teams deployed by the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in Besse, responded promptly to restore peace and prevent further carnage. However, three Fulani people lost their lives, while a police inspector sustained injuries in the line of duty," he said.

The state police spokesman said a tactical team of the police had been deployed to the troubled communities and normalcy is gradually returning to the area.

"The police have launched investigation into the attack and is following up on the attackers," he said.

'Attacks sign of frustration'

A security expert, who retired as a Captain in the Nigerian Army, Shehu Abubakar, told our correspondent that the attacks carried out by suspected members of the Lakurawa group in some communities of Kebbi, is a sign of frustration.

"You should understand that a battalion of the Nigerian Army was recently established at Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government to curtail activities of the bandits and Lakurawa, operating in the area. The Lakurawa must leave the area to find a convenient place as base to carry out their attacks. They carried out their attack on the communities along the River Niger bank while migrating to another area to avenge the presence of the army base at Kaoje.

"They can no longer stay close to the area where the battalion is located. They migrated from Kaoje, through the bank of the River Niger, moving through communities of Samanaji, Dutsinmari, Zaria Kalakala, to where they started their attacks at Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi. Now that they seem to have been displaced, the security agencies operating in the state should follow them up in every move they make so that they don't get a convenient place to settle. That way, they may be frustrated to move out of the state," he said.

Military bases in Kebbi

In the last two years, six Forward Operation Bases were established in Sakaba,Zuru,Yauri, Augie and Kaoje. The Battalion in Birnin Kebbi was upgraded to an Armoured Brigade, just as there is a battalion in Zuru.There are also army units in parts of Kaoje and other areas to strengthen military operations in the troubled communities of Augie, Danko Wasagu, Mahuta, Argungu, Arewa, Bagudo and Dandi, but the spate of killings occasioned by bandits and Lakurawa attacks remain a growing concern among residents.

Close 

Kebbi's killing fields

On Wednesday of last week, a large number of bandits invaded Dirin -Daji in Sakara Local Government Area of the state. It took the combined efforts of the security agencies in the area to disperse the attackers.

A week before the Kaoje district attack, three people were killed at Kasabo, a community in Saminaka, Yauri Local Government Area of the state. The community was attacked by the bandits in the early hours of the day when people were preparing to go about their daily activities. A resident, Aminu Usman, said their attackers came in large number to invade the community and that they killed three people while many others escaped through the bush.

A few days before the attack at Kasabo, suspected members of the Lakurawa terrorists group attacked the site of the construction company handling the Badagry-Ilela Supper Highway project at Gubba in Maiyama Local Government Area of the state, killing two soldiers and a Chinese national. The attackers were said to have crossed into Kebbi from Kebbe area of Sokoto, to carry out the attack, it was gathered.

Efforts to get comments from the state government proved abortive, but a top government official who does not want his name in print told our corespondent that the state government was working closely with security agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for the attacks.

He said, "Governor Nasir Idris has been up and doing on issues of security on the state. No fewer than 109 armoured vehicles and other logistics have been procured for security agencies to fight insecurity in the state."

World.title: Africa: AFCON Every Two Years Again As CAF Reverses Decision
World.content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-year cycle.

The decision was unanimously approved by the CAF Executive Committee, with President Patrice Motsepe announcing the development after the organisation's Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026.

The reversal comes after CAF reviewed its earlier plan to move AFCON to a four-year schedule and introduce an Africa Nations League as a biennial competition.

CAF said the proposed Nations League would take several years to generate the financial resources and football development benefits required to make its competitions globally competitive and financially sustainable.



In a statement published on its website on Thursday, Motsepe said the decision to retain the two-year AFCON cycle was taken in the interest of African football, the confederation's 54 member associations and African players playing for clubs outside the continent.

"The decision by the CAF EXCO that the CAF AFCON should take place every Two Years was based on advancing, protecting and promoting the interest of African Football and CAF's 54 Member Associations, as well as the interest of African players employed by Football Clubs outside Africa," he said.

Motsepe added that CAF was concerned about the time it would take for the proposed Africa Nations League to deliver the financial and developmental gains initially expected from the competition.

He said the new tournament was intended to mirror the existing AFCON format and take place every two years, but would not provide the required support for African football in the immediate future.

Under the revised calendar, the next AFCON will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament.

The subsequent editions are scheduled for 2028, 2031 and 2033, with CAF maintaining that the competition will not be staged in a FIFA World Cup year.

Motsepe expressed confidence in the three East African countries' ability to deliver a successful tournament in 2027.

He also described AFCON as more than a football competition, saying it provides an opportunity to celebrate Africa's cultures and bring people from across the continent and the diaspora together.

"The AFCON competition is also about celebrating African Football and Africa's rich and diverse cultures, customs and traditions and bringing people together from Africa's 54 Countries, the African Diaspora and throughout the world," he said.

"The CAF EXCO decision is in the best interest of African Football and CAF's 54 Member Associations and will also contribute significantly to the development and growth of football in Africa," he added.

World.title: South Africa: African Horse Sickness Confirmed in Western Cape's Cederberg
World.content:
The Department of Agriculture has confirmed a case of African horse sickness (AHS) in a single horse on a property in the Cederberg Local Municipality in the Western Cape, prompting movement restrictions and intensified surveillance to contain the disease.

Laboratory tests conducted by the University of Pretoria's Veterinary Genetics Laboratory confirmed the presence of AHS virus serotype 7 on the property, which is located within South Africa's established AHS Protection Zone.

Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp said the case was detected through the country's veterinary surveillance systems, enabling authorities to respond swiftly and implement containment measures.

"The swift detection of this case in the Cederberg Local Municipality is a good example of how South Africa's veterinary surveillance system works. As a result, the authorities were able to move quickly to the affected area and take the required stringent actions as stipulated in the Animal Diseases Act and deploy containment protocols," Aucamp said.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

In accordance with the Animal Diseases Act, 1984 (Act 35 of 1984), and the Western Cape Department of Agriculture's AHS contingency plan, an outbreak containment area has been established and movement controls implemented.

Horse movements within the controlled area ordinarily require a permit issued by the State Veterinarian: Boland. However, the department has advised that no permits will be issued for moving horses out of the affected area, while investigations and surveillance continue.

Veterinary Services, working with authorised veterinarians and industry partners, have also commenced intensive surveillance, tracing and census activities to determine the extent of the outbreak and identify any additional cases.

The department has urged equine owners in the controlled area to cooperate with Veterinary Services and report any animals showing signs consistent with AHS, including unexplained fever, swelling of the head or neck, breathing difficulties or sudden death.

Horse owners are also encouraged to take precautions against Culicoides midges, which transmit the disease. Recommended measures include stabling horses, where possible, from two hours before sunset until two hours after sunrise, avoiding low-lying and wet areas, and appropriately using registered insect repellents and insecticides.

The department has strongly discouraged AHS vaccination at this time, explaining that the currently registered vaccine is live-attenuated and that vaccination during periods of vector activity could result in the vaccine strain being spread by midges, potentially worsening the situation.

Close 

"While there is no proof of large-scale disease activity outside the said property, the department is focused on total vigilance and calls on all horse owners to refrain from AHS vaccination during this period. Veterinary Services will continue to monitor the situation closely and will provide updates as additional information becomes available," Aucamp said.

The department said international trade partners will be notified of the outbreak, with further information on the implications for international trade to be provided in due course.

Updates on containment measures, movement restrictions and permits will be issued by the Western Cape Department of Agriculture. Further information is available from Veterinary Services and at www.myhorse.org.za

World.title: Kenya: No, Kenyan Pastor Victor Kanyari Was Not Killed in a Road Accident
World.content:
No, Kenyan pastor Victor Kanyari was not killed in a road accident

IN SHORT: A fake Citizen Digital news graphic claims Kenyan pastor Victor Kanyari died in a road accident. But the image is fabricated and uses an old photograph of a separate crash.

Social media posts circulating in Kenya feature what appears to be a Citizen Digital breaking news alert, dated 5 October 2026. It claims that pastor Victor Kanyari has died in a road accident along Kangundo Road in the capital, Nairobi.



The graphic shows Kanyari alongside a badly damaged white vehicle surrounded by onlookers.

Collectively, the posts we sampled received more than 162,000 views and 2,000 likes.

Who is Kanyari?

Kanyari is a Kenyan preacher who heads the Salvation Healing Ministry in Nairobi. He made headlines in 2014 after a KTN investigation exposed staged miracles at his ministry and his controversial KSh310 donation scheme, which he later acknowledged was intended to lift him out of poverty.

Kanyari was previously married to gospel singer Beatrice Wairimu Mbugua, popularly known as Betty Bayo. They had two children. Bayo died of leukaemia on 10 November 2025, prompting a custody dispute between Kanyari and the children's stepfather, Hiram Gitau, popularly known as Tash.

On 26 October 2026, a court awarded Kanyari legal custody but ordered a gradual transition, allowing the children to remain temporarily with Tash.

The dispute, along with his active social media presence, has kept Kanyari in the public eye. He has also announced plans to contest the Kasarani parliamentary seat in Kenya's 2027 general election.

Citizen Digital is the online news platform of Citizen TV, owned by Royal Media Services.

But did the broadcaster report Kanyari's death in a road accident? We checked.

Old accident photo used in fake graphic

We found no credible news reports confirming Kanyari's alleged death or a corresponding report on Citizen Digital or Citizen TV's social media accounts.

In contrast, Kanyari's social media accounts feature recent photos and videos of him going about his usual activities.

A reverse image search revealed that the photo of the wrecked vehicle had been shared on Facebook on 27 June 2024, more than two years before the supposed news alert.

Close 

The earlier post was captioned: "Bad accident on Ngong road joining on to Karen road. Multiple casualties."

The vehicle and onlookers match those in the circulating graphic, confirming the photograph predates the alleged October 2026 crash.

The graphic is fabricated. It uses an old accident photo to support a false claim about Kanyari's death. His recent public activities also contradict the rumour.

World.title: Kenya: 46 Ebola Contacts Set for Discharge From Quarantine On November 3
World.content:
Nairobi — Public Health Principal Secretary May Muthoni says 46 contacts under quarantine are expected to be discharged on November 3 after completing the required monitoring period.

Muthoni has directed health teams to prepare the necessary discharge packages and support for those completing quarantine.

"We must also be able to complete the full 21 days of followup and every person leaving quarantine must receive the agreed discharge package and support... we must also continue to follow up the nine contacts outside Kenya with the countries concerned," she said.



She said every person leaving quarantine must receive the agreed assistance as authorities maintain surveillance to prevent further transmission.

The PS urged response teams to ensure all arrangements are in place ahead of Tuesday's planned discharge.

"Kenya is making progress in containing the Ebola outbreak, with no new cases reported in the last 10 days, following coordinated efforts by the Ministry of Health, County Governments and development partners," Muthoni stated.

So far, the country has recorded nine cases and two deaths;.

Following confirmation of the first Ebola case on 6 October, the health ministry conducted "robust contact tracing of anyone who may have been exposed", the World Health Organization (WHO) says. By 22 October, all contacts had been traced, both in Kenya and internationally, and placed in quarantine, it adds.

The government says that the confirmed cases so far are connected and there is no evidence that the virus has spread to the community.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Kill Four in Plateau Community Despite Curfew
World.content:
The attackers reportedly stormed the community at about 8 p.m. and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to contain insecurity.

At least four people were killed after gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night.

The attackers reportedly stormed the community at about 8 p.m. and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to contain insecurity.



A resident of Barkin Ladi, Bulus Jok, said the gunmen operated freely for some time, shooting indiscriminately.

"The gunmen struck the community around 8 p.m. despite the curfew in place and started shooting sporadically," Mr Jok said.

He added that the attack threw residents into panic, leaving four people dead.

Mr Jok expressed concern that the incident occurred despite an early warning reportedly sent to relevant authorities a day before the attack.

"It is very sad, especially as there had been an early warning alert sent to the relevant authorities a day before the attack," he said.

The Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the incident.

Mr Tengwong condemned the killings, describing the attack as unacceptable and expressing concern over the continued assaults on communities despite security measures.

He urged security agencies to intensify surveillance, strengthen their presence in vulnerable communities and respond promptly to intelligence and early warning reports to prevent further attacks.

The latest incident adds to the series of attacks on communities in Plateau State, raising fresh concerns about the effectiveness of security measures, including curfews, in protecting residents.

Efforts to reach security operatives for official confirmation and further details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

World.title: Ohio State's national title hopes are rightfully fading after USC delivers reality check in shocking upset
World.content:
If the Big Ten was resting their hopes on Ohio State being able to put together an offense capable of contending for a national championship, then Saturday night's 30-18 loss to USC was a reality check on the current situation.

Following the unfortunate loss of starting quarterback Julian Sayin to an elbow injury during the Indiana game two weeks ago, the fate of the Buckeyes season rested on the arms of Luke Fahey and freshman Taven St. Clair.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

The nervousness around Columbus has been rampant since that day in Bloomington, and rightfully so given that Ryan Day had pinned his offensive hopes around the quarterback being able to disrupt opposing defenses with the Julian Sayin to Jeremiah Smith connection.

GOOD LUCK, SEC: AUBURN AWOKE A MONSTER IN ATHENS, AND FLORIDA PAYS THE PRICE IN GEORGIA’S COCKTAIL BEATDOWN

This pair opened up so many options for an offense that essentially forced opposing teams to decide on whether double-teaming the star wide receiver was worth the risk in losing a defender in the secondary.

Even with 484 yards of total offense against USC on Saturday night, it was the offensive line that struggled to protect quarterback Luke Fahey, while also not capitalizing inside the red zone.

You might ask whether one player is worth that much attention. To that, most college football fans would just implore you to "watch the tape" on the former Heisman Trophy leader coming out of the Indiana showdown that saw the Buckeyes leave Bloomington with a very important win.

Now, a few weeks later, there are rightful questions about this Ohio State team moving forward over the next month, along with where the Big Ten stands as we await the first CFP rankings of the 2026 season.

The answer to that question centered around the fact Ohio State had not scored a touchdown against USC through three quarters, and they looked like a squad who was lost on offense for a majority of this upset loss.

OHIO STATE QB JULIAN SAYIN'S INJURY MAY COMPLETELY RESHAPE THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RACE

Does Ohio State look like a national title contender without Julian Sayin?

No, not right now after two weeks of preparation for the trip to Los Angeles.

If anything, the Buckeyes look like a team that would be on the brink of missing the playoff tonight if Indiana were to have somehow won that intense showdown.

So yes, Ohio State fans are clearly entering the panic mode of what could have been if Julian Sayin were to not have been injured.

Also, let's not forget the other unfortunate part of this problem for the Buckeyes. Entering the matchup with Indiana, Jeremiah Smith was the proverbial leader in the clubhouse for the Heisman Trophy. Now, he's going to need plenty of superman-like efforts to have his name called in New York City next month, without a quarterback capable enough to get him the ball downfield.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL CHAOS: HISTORIC UPSETS, ARCH MANNING'S FIASCO, CLOCK CONTROVERSY AND CFP RAMIFICATIONS ARISE

Sure, we know Smith is a man of high character and is more worried about the wins and losses. But, let's not act as though the situation isn’t a brutal dose of reality that his campaign might have ended in Bloomington.

Fittingly, it was Jeremiah Smith who scored Ohio State's first touchdown of the night with 2:12 remaining in the game on a five-yard out in the end zone.

As for Ohio State moving forward, there is nothing about their performance against USC that should give the CFP committee enough evidence to put them in the top-12 on Tuesday night.

We all remember when Florida State was left out of the national championship game after Jordan Travis went down with a knee injury, right?

No, we aren’t at that point just yet, but we're getting there. Over the next five weeks, Ohio State will face Northwestern, Oregon, Nebraska and Michigan.

INDIANA SURVIVES MINNESOTA SCARE WITH SECOND STRAIGHT OVERTIME WIN TO KEEP NATIONAL TITLE DEFENSE ALIVE

Are we going to act as though this Buckeyes offense is good enough to avoid another loss? Sure, you can make that argument, but Oregon and Northwestern are talented enough to beat them in Columbus, and Nebraska is so awkward that it could have a lead heading into the fourth quarter.

The Buckeyes defense isn’t strong enough to carry them through the month of November, especially if this is what they are going to get from the offensive side of the ball.

And unfortunately, Jeremiah Smith and running back Bo Jackson can't do it all without a viable quarterback that oozes confidence.

Lincoln Riley finds himself on the winning side, with a tough stretch ahead

Give credit where it's due with this USC football team.

Coming off a loss to Wisconsin this week, with reasonable conversations surrounding his job status with the Trojans, the talk of Riley coaching somewhere else next season started picking up enough that he could not avoid the questions over the past five days.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Now, there is at least a path to the postseason, though it won't be an easy one.

After a week off, USC will play Indiana on the road, followed by a game against Maryland, before ending the season with a crosstown showdown with UCLA.

Can they run the table? Sure, if this is the type of performance we get over the next month.

But, even with the win over Ohio State, it's still hard to trust the Trojans. They’re going to have to prove it.

World.title: Bill Belichick's UNC Tar Heels nearly upset top-ranked Miami before costly strip-sack
World.content:
Bill Belichick, the day his UNC Tar Heels were set to face the No. 1 Miami Hurricanes in Chapel Hill, was the center of more off-field noise regarding his relationship.

This time, though, it was reported the 74-year-old actually ended things with 25-year-old Jordon Hudson over a year ago, per TMZ. They remain "committed to their business partnerships" and "remain close friends."

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Nonetheless, a game had to be played, and Belichick and UNC were certainly not thinking about his relationship status. They wanted to give Miami a run for their money.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Tar Heels came close to upsetting the Hurricanes, but they ran out of gas in the fourth quarter in a 38-35 loss to move to 4-4 on the season. Miami stayed undefeated, improving to 8-0 on the year and 6-0 in ACC play.

No one expected Belichick's squad to be able to handle the Hurricanes, led by Mario Cristobal. But just as Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah continued his efficient play this season, Billy Edwards Jr. was matching him when the Tar Heels had the ball.

Edwards threw for 341 yards on 28-of-34 through the air with four touchdown passes, including a 16-yard strike to Jordan Shipp to take a 21-17 lead — UNC’s first of the game — in the third quarter.

From there, both teams were trading blows, and the lead, on the scoreboard. Miami responded with an 80-yard drive to retake their lead, 24-21, but UNC continued to fight on while crushing clock heading into the fourth quarter.

Edwards led a 16-play, 75-yard drive capped with a touchdown run by Demon June from one yard out. There was a lot of time left in this ballgame, which Miami knew despite some shock of what UNC was doing to them at home.

Mensah wasn’t fazed, though, as yet another touchdown drive came from the Hurricanes thanks to key catch-and-runs, including a 31-yard burst from star receiver Malachi Toney. Mark Fletcher Jr. regained the Miami lead with a two-yard run and 7:49 left on the clock.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The way this game was going, it seemed Belichick and UNC would have a chance if they were able to get the ball last. However, a grave error slammed the door shut on those chances.

Edwards was strip-sacked by Marquise Lightfoot, and Miami recovered at the UNC 37-yard line. That was the defensive stop needed to swing the tides of momentum, and Mensah didn’t thwart that opportunity.

Toney caught a nine-yard touchdown pass from his quarterback, and with a 10-point lead with 2:33 left to go, it was eventually the separation needed to leave Chapel Hill without Miami’s record being blemished. But it didn’t come without sweating until the end.

UNC would score on the ensuing possession to make things interesting, as Edwards threw for his fourth touchdown of the game with 1:38 left to play. Then, needing to recover an onside kick, the Tar Heels actually came away with it — until a yellow flag was seen on the turf. Offsides was called.

On the second try, UNC recovered again, but another flag negated it as a Tar Heels player hit the Miami player trying to recover the ball before crossing the necessary 10 yards.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

The third try was finally recovered by the Hurricanes, and they ran the clock out.

Mensah threw for 274 yards and three scores, while rushing for 36 yards. Toney had two of those touchdowns, hauling in seven receptions for 75 yards. Fletcher also scored three total touchdowns.

World.title: BYU survives unranked Arizona State's second-half rally, stays unbeaten at home

Eighth-ranked BYU pulled away after Arizona State rallied to tie the game at 17 late in the third quarter. Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier threw for 236 yards and a touchdown to help secure the 27-20 victory.

The Cougars blanked the Sun Devils in the fourth quarter. After a 45-yard field goal put BYU ahead for good, running back Sione Moa scored from 1 yard out to seal the victory with just over two minutes remaining.

TRANSFER PORTAL, NOT NIL, REASON FOR PARITY, CLAIMS COLLEGE FOOTBALL EXPERT BROOKS AUSTIN

Fette threw two third-quarter touchdown passes as Arizona State erased a 14-point deficit. The Sun Devils converted three third downs on their first scoring drive, which ended with Omarion Miller’s 20-yard touchdown catch. BYU QB BEAR BACHMEIER SAYS NOTRE DAME 'DISRESPECTED' HIM AND HIS FAMILY FOLLOWING UPSET WIN OVER IRISH

He fumbled on the third play of Arizona State’s opening drive. Isaiah Glasker pounced on the ball at the Sun Devil 29, setting up BYU’s first touchdown.

World.title: Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream fall short in Game 7 as Golden State Valkyries win first WNBA championship
World.content:
SAN FRANCISCO – Angel Reese scored one point and did not attempt a field goal in the fourth quarter of Game 7. The Atlanta Dream needed more from her with a championship on the line.

The Golden State Valkyries beat Atlanta 68-63 on Saturday night at Chase Center, winning the best-of-seven WNBA Finals 4-3 to claim the franchise’s first championship.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Reese finished with eight points on 3-for-7 shooting, 12 rebounds and four turnovers. It was her fourth consecutive game with more turnovers than made field goals. Across those four games, she shot 12-for-45 (26.7%) and committed 19 turnovers.

USA SPORTS, NBC CLAIM RECORD WNBA FINALS RATINGS, BUT COMPARISONS LEAVE OUT IMPORTANT CONTEXT

Golden State guard Gabby Williams delivered the performance Atlanta needed from its star. She was named Finals MVP after scoring 30 points, including 28 in the second half, and blocking four shots in the clincher. Her 31-foot three-pointer with 2:18 remaining broke a 57-57 tie and put Golden State ahead for good.

Reese’s only point in the final period came on a free throw with 18.6 seconds remaining.

Before tipoff, both teams again left the court for the national anthem, completing the seven-game series without appearing on the floor for any of the performances.

WNBA FINALS TEAMS END SEASON WITH ONE FINAL NATIONAL ANTHEM SNUB AS DREAM, VALKYRIES LEAVE COURT

Reese’s Finals had looked much different when Atlanta held a 2-1 series lead.

She combined for 51 points and 28 rebounds in Games 2 and 3, then explained how she believed she was getting into Golden State’s head.

"They’re playing into my mental game where I can take their confidence and just try to do whatever to mess them up," Reese said before Game 4.

The Valkyries won the next two games. Atlanta forced Game 7 with an 80-69 victory Thursday behind Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard’s combined 44 points, but Reese continued to struggle with her shooting, making five of 18 attempts.

She finished the final four games with 38 points, 13 fewer than she scored in Games 2 and 3 combined.

Saturday offered a chance to finish the series differently. Instead, Jordin Canada carried Atlanta’s offense for much of the night, while Reese never became a scoring factor down the stretch.

The Dream went scoreless for the first 5:19 as Golden State built an 8-0 lead. Reese finally put Atlanta on the board with a basket off an offensive rebound.

Atlanta recovered to trail just 14-12 after one quarter, and Reese’s three-pointer early in the second gave the Dream their first lead.

Canada scored 11 points in the second quarter and had 13 at halftime. Golden State went more than eight minutes without a field goal to begin the period, allowing Atlanta to take a 30-24 lead into the break.

Reese had five points, seven rebounds and three turnovers at halftime. Williams had just two points.

The Dream extended their lead to 37-28 midway through the third quarter. Then Williams took over.

She scored Golden State’s final 13 points of the period, including three three-pointers in a 56-second span. Reese answered one of those threes with a hook through contact, but missed the accompanying free throw. It was her last basket of the night.

Williams’ turnaround jumper with 1:05 remaining gave the Valkyries a 45-44 lead entering the fourth. She scored 15 points in the quarter and added 13 more in the final period.

Allisha Gray’s two free throws tied the game at 55 with 3:15 left. Williams answered with a driving layup. Howard tied it again at 57 before Williams buried the three from 31 feet.

After Gray missed a wide-open layup, Williams made two free throws to push Golden State’s lead to five with 1:40 remaining.

Kiah Stokes then delivered on the offensive glass. She rebounded two consecutive Williams misses, converting the second into a putback that stretched the lead to 64-57 with 53.8 seconds left.

Gray’s three-pointer brought Atlanta within four, but Tiffany Hayes answered with two free throws.

Reese grabbed an offensive rebound and drew a foul with 18.6 seconds remaining. She missed the first free throw and made the second, leaving Atlanta down five.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

She then stole a Williams pass, and Gray made two free throws to cut the deficit to 66-63 with 10.5 seconds left. Veronica Burton’s two free throws with 5.1 seconds remaining secured the victory.

Stokes finished with eight points, 13 rebounds and two blocks. Burton added 10 points and 11 rebounds, while Hayes scored 11.

Canada led Atlanta with 18 points, and Gray added 16. Howard finished with six points on 3-for-14 shooting, missing all seven of her three-point attempts. The Dream shot 33.3% overall and went 6-for-30 from beyond the arc.

Reese finished the series averaging 14.7 points and 12.9 rebounds while shooting 40.5% from the field.

After Game 3, she had explained how she measures greatness.

"I think you become one of the greats … when you can win and impact winning," Reese said.

She helped put Atlanta two wins from a championship. Across the final four games, she didn't do enough for the Dream to finish the job.

World.title: Paul Skenes and Livvy Dunne's Halloween costume will enrage anyone tired of rushing through holidays
World.content:
I hope you had a great Halloween. I know I did, handing out candy to the two trick-or-treaters who stopped at my house.

And to the kids who walked by my house without stopping, the joke is on you: I now have a giant bowl of Twizzlers, Reese's and Jolly Ranchers to shame-eat for the next couple of days.

And plenty of athletes seemed to have a great holiday too, including Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes and his girlfriend Livvy Dunne.

CARDINALS' BUDDA BAKER FIELDS QUESTIONS ABOUT TRADE RUMORS WHILE WEARING EVIL CLOWN HALLOWEEN MASK

But their costume choice is alarming for those of us who want to savor Halloween before we start looking not one, but two holidays ahead.

The couple shared photos and video of their costumes: Buddy the Elf of "Elf" fame and a bottle of Mrs. Butterworth's syrup.

It's a solid costume, as Will Ferrell's iconic character is big on syrup, but... CHRISTMAS?!?!

Like, not even Neal Page and Del Griffith from "Planes, Trains, and Automobiles" would tell Halloween to pound sand, skip Thanksgiving like some soulless red-headed holiday stepchild and go straight to Christmas.

It kind of reminds me of a Halloween I had a couple of years ago. I was working in my office that afternoon and watching 1933's "The Invisible Man" when I heard my wife digging for something in the closet.

MAGGIE SAJAK LOOKS LIKE A MILLION BUCKS FOR HALLOWEEN, BILLY NAPIER MAKES HORRIBLE HISTORY & TIM DUNCAN VOTES!

Moments later, she walked out with our Christmas tree and set it up before the Invisible Man even left the Lion's Head Inn.

I'm not a hard-and-fast "Christmas must wait until after-Thanksgiving" guy. I'll hum a Christmas carol or steal a mini candy cane from a bank teller's desk before Thanksgiving Day, but I never go full-Christmas until I awake from my Thanksgiving food coma.

Not Skenes and Dunne, though. They’re already in Christmas mode while people across the country are still dressing as the woman from "Obsession," donning inflatable Minion costumes and waiting to take their first Halloween Jell-O shot.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

I mean, great costume work, but let's savor Halloween before we have to start thinking about buying everyone in our family Amazon gift cards.

The attack occurred around 8 p.m. near Shore Parkway and Bay 17th Street in Brooklyn's Bath Beach neighborhood, according to the New York Police Department.

Police said the woman was jogging eastbound along the Shore Parkway Greenway when she suffered multiple stab wounds to the neck.

Emergency medical personnel transported her to NYU Langone Hospital-Brooklyn in critical condition.

MAN DEAD, ANOTHER CRITICAL AFTER DOUBLE STABBING AT BROOKLYN PARK AS POLICE DETAIN PERSON OF INTEREST: NYPD

An NYPD spokesperson confirmed to Fox News Digital on Saturday that the woman remained alive.

Police have not released her identity, and investigators have not identified a suspect, the spokesperson said.

The New York Post reported that the woman had been training for Sunday's New York City Marathon, citing police sources.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, New York Road Runners (NYRR), which organizes the marathon, expressed sympathy for the victim and her family.

GEORGIA JOGGER RUNS FOR HER LIFE AFTER STRANGER ALLEGEDLY TRIES TO MOW HER DOWN 3 TIMES

The fourth-ranked Indiana Hoosiers escaped again on Saturday.

World.title: WNBA Finals teams end season with one final national anthem snub as Dream, Valkyries leave court
World.content:
SAN FRANCISCO – The WNBA Finals went the full seven games. And the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries stayed off the court for the national anthem before every one of them.

Both teams left the floor before Saturday night’s deciding game at Chase Center, completing a series-long pattern that continued despite criticism and repeated questions about why their pregame routines take them off the court during the performance.

Saturday’s anthem was performed by San Francisco’s Glide Ensemble. The choir’s website describes its music as "steeped in protest and visions of a more just and loving world" and says it spreads a message of "diversity, acceptance and love."

Not even a radically left-wing church choir could get the players to stand on the court for two minutes during the anthem.

WNBA PLAYERS, COACHES REFUSE TO EXPLAIN NATIONAL ANTHEM ABSENCES AMID MOUNTING CRITICISM

The league’s first Game 7 came after Atlanta’s 80–69 victory Thursday evened the series at 3–3.

Saturday’s winner will claim its franchise’s first WNBA championship.

Two weeks after OutKick first asked why the teams were leaving the floor for the anthem, the WNBA, NBA and both teams’ front offices still have not answered our questions. Players and coaches have pointed to their pregame routines.

Seven games, same pregame routine

The performers and venues changed. The teams’ absence from the court did not.

Alanis Morissette sang before Game 2 at Chase Center. On Thursday in Atlanta, 10-year-old Heiress Harris, the daughter of rapper T.I., performed before Game 6. Both teams were off the floor for those performances.

When OutKick finally had an opportunity to question players and coaches directly at media availability in Atlanta on Oct. 23, Golden State coach Natalie Nakase said the practice was part of pregame.

"We’re two years in," Nakase said. "That’s been part of our pregame."

Asked who established the routine and why, Nakase said, "I really don’t know."

"I understand your question," she added. "I’m not trying to, you know, not answer your question. It’s just part of our pregame."

OutKick followed up: "What do you do during those 90 seconds that you’re off the court?"

"I’m with my staff, so I’m focused on my plays," Nakase said.

Golden State’s public relations staff then moved to the next reporter. OutKick did not get an opportunity to ask why those preparations needed to happen during the anthem rather than before or afterward.

Valkyries forward Gabby Williams denied that Golden State’s absence was a protest.

"No," Williams said.

Asked why the team was off the court, she responded: "That’s been the routine for like, seven years now."

A Valkyries public relations representative then said, "Next question."

Golden State is in its second season. Williams previously played for Chicago and Seattle, but did not explain whether each team followed the same routine.

OUTKICK READERS BLAST WNBA PLAYERS FOR HIDING DURING FINALS NATIONAL ANTHEM

Atlanta coach Karl Smesko offered less detail when asked why his team left the court and whose decision it was.

"We’re just kind of focused on the Finals," Smesko said.

Asked whether he had any further comment about the anthem and his team’s absences, he said, "No."

Howard defended Team USA commitment as fans offered different views

Dream guard Rhyne Howard was asked about calls to exclude players from Team USA over their anthem conduct during the WNBA season.

"I don’t think I’ve been on the floor for the national anthem for any of my tenure in Atlanta, so if that’s what people are gonna look to nitpick for then so be it," Howard said.

"But as far as competing for your team, when I go put on USA jersey I’m out for the national anthem every time, there’s no doubt about it."

"Yes, I love the country that I play for and I love what we have here," she added.

When OutKick asked why she was not on the court for the anthem with the Dream, Howard and an Atlanta public relations representative both responded, "Next question."

VANCE CONDEMNS 'DISGRACEFUL' WNBA NATIONAL ANTHEM WALKOUTS, SAYS PLAYERS SHOULD SHOW MORE GRATITUDE

Fans who spoke with OutKick outside State Farm Arena before Game 6 disagreed about whether the players should be on the floor.

Renard Hayes, the father of Golden State guard Tiffany Hayes, pointed to his own military service while defending the players’ choice.

"This is America, by the way, and I’ve served this country, so they can choose what they want," he said.

"I don’t have an issue with it because it’s not a disrespect of the flag," Hayes added.

A male Valkyries fan said he respected the players’ opinions and beliefs but wanted them on the court.

"I do think they should be out there," he said.

Another Dream fan defended the practice: "They’ve been doing it for years. And that’s their choice. It is what it is."

Rulebook provision remains as policy questions go unanswered

The WNBA’s 2026 official rulebook says players, coaches and trainers are to "stand and line up in a dignified posture" along the sidelines or on the foul line during the national anthem.

The Associated Press reported Oct. 20 that the league suspended its anthem protocols in 2017. The provision remains in the 2026 rulebook.

OutKick has asked the WNBA to clarify its current requirements and enforcement, whether discipline was planned or under consideration, and whether the league had communicated instructions to either team.

The inquiries to the WNBA, Dream and Valkyries began after Game 1 on Oct. 17, with follow-ups Oct. 18 and Oct. 20. OutKick also contacted the NBA league office on Oct. 20 about its role in the matter.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

The Oct. 23 interviews were OutKick’s first opportunity to put the anthem questions directly to players and coaches after attending all 13 formal press conferences during the first three games without being called on.

OutKick also asked Atlanta to confirm an arena employee’s account that Dream players stand in a hallway after leaving the floor before games, including whether they remain there during the anthem. The team did not respond.

During Game 4, I attempted to observe what Atlanta’s players do after leaving the court. Arena staff said my credential did not grant access to that area and escorted me to my assigned media seat.

One team will leave Saturday night with a championship. Both will finish the season having stayed off the court for every national anthem in the Finals.

World.title: Alaska officials ask judge to deny DOJ’s ‘impossible’ demand to set aside ballots
World.content:
The Republican-led state government in Alaska implored a federal judge on Saturday to permanently dismiss the Trump administration’s lawsuit that seeks to block the certification of the Alaska Senate race if GOP Sen. Dan S. Sullivan loses.

“The United States’ opposition provides no reason for this Court to entertain this meritless lawsuit any longer,” the filing said, adding that “the relief demanded is inappropriate and not even possible given Alaskan voters’ vital right to ballot secrecy.”

The filing from Alaska officials comes just three days before Election Day and as the judge is expected to rule soon on whether to dismiss the lawsuit or continue with it.

The Trump administration has claimed that Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola’s campaign was involved in recruiting a retired teacher with the same name as Sullivan to run in the race, creating confusion that it says will unfairly take away votes intended for the incumbent. Peltola has denied the allegations.

The Trump administration filed a lawsuit Oct. 22 against local election officials, arguing that the results of the competitive Senate race should not be certified unless Sen. Dan S. Sullivan is declared the winner.

Alaska officials on Saturday criticized the legal basis on which the Trump administration has argued it has standing to intervene in the election, as election certification is left up to the states.

The filing noted that the Alaska Supreme Court approved the second Sullivan’s name to be on the ballot months ago and added that “state officials carefully designed the ballot to minimize voter confusion.”

Alaska officials also took aim at the Justice Department’s proposal of “segregating” ballots that rank Dan J. Sullivan, writing, “this unexplained idea makes no sense.”

“No matter how the ballots are physically stored, it will be easy to tell which ballots rank Daniel J.,” the filing said. “If the United States means something different — as it seems to — its ballot segregation proposal is both disturbing and impossible.”

The Alaska attorney general’s office asked the judge to “immediately dismiss this lawsuit with prejudice and allow state officials to conduct the general election — including ballot counting and certification — free from unwarranted federal interference.”

The Trump administration amended its complaint this week to cite new reporting from The New York Times, which alleged that Peltola’s campaign was involved in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan and that Peltola herself was aware of the situation. The Times story citied a former campaign manager who later attempted to retract her statements.

At a rally Friday night, Peltola told a crowd of her supporters that she was “so deeply offended by these accusations about having any involvement with anyone else’s candidacy.”

“I want fewer candidates in the primary. I’m not out soliciting more competition,” Peltola said, adding she did “not need any help” defeating Sen. Dan S. Sullivan.

Sen. Dan S. Sullivan took aim at Peltola in a Fox News interview on Saturday, saying that “there’s no way Peltola doesn’t know about” the scheme to recruit Dan J. Sullivan.

“It’s deception. But at its worst, it’s disdain for us Alaskans,” he said. “Think about what they did. They’re trying to make sure that Alaskans throw away their vote.”

World.title: Democrats in key battlegrounds throw Joe Biden under the bus on the border
World.content:
WASHINGTON — Democratic candidates in 2026 battleground races are directly criticizing Joe Biden’s handling of border security when he was president, seeking to neutralize a political vulnerability and signaling a new path for the party on the thorny issue.

Candidates are throwing the ex-president under the bus on border policy in key states that will decide control of the Senate and some battleground House races across the country.

“I called out Joe Biden for failing us on the border,” Texas’ Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico says in a recent ad airing in the closing stretch of his neck-and-neck race against Republican Ken Paxton. He also criticized Biden in July for having “failed us on our southern border” as he rolled out his own border security plan.

He’s not alone.

In Kansas, a longtime Republican stronghold, Democrat Adam Hamilton criticized Biden in a recent debate with Republican Sen. Roger Marshall.

“I want to be crystal clear, first of all: Immigration at the border under Biden was a disaster. That is how we ended up where we are today,” he said. “Second, what we did in response to that has been a disaster for people across the state of Kansas.”

Hamilton, like other Democrats in areas that voted for Trump in 2024, paired their critique of Biden with criticism that the current president has gone too far on enforcement. Polls show many Americans have soured on Trump’s handling of the issue in the wake of immigration officers fatally shooting two Americans in Minnesota and one in Maine this year.

Still, the comments reflect a recognition that the issue of border security remains a vulnerability for Democrats as Republicans continue to accuse them of promoting “open borders” in a bid to mobilize their base and win swing voters. Biden’s ratings on the issue tanked amid a surge in migrant crossings during his presidency, which Trump successfully weaponized in 2024.

Entering office in 2021, Biden inherited a Covid-era migration surge that intensified in the United States after he made good on his pledge to roll back Trump-era policies and restrictions, allowing more asylum-seekers to stay in the country as their cases were being considered. The collective result was a huge spike in border crossings that became associated with the Biden presidency and brought down his approval ratings.

Even as Trump’s approval rating has fallen to 38%, polls show border security continues to be one of his highest-polling issues, although that number has fallen from the highs of his early second term.

“The Biden administration failed at the border,” Democratic House candidate Paige Cognetti said at a debate Thursday night.

Cognetti, who is vying to unseat Rep. Rob Bresnahan, R-Pa., in a highly competitive Scranton-area working-class district, later added: “The Biden administration did fail. We need to make sure that the border is secure. It’s a good thing that it is. We do need to make sure that the pathways to citizenship are there.”

In South Carolina, Democratic Senate candidate Annie Andrews said in a debate, “Democrats have failed on the border.”

Democratic pollster Celinda Lake said it’s “very smart” for candidates to distance themselves from Biden and that “there’s nobody contesting that interpretation” that he blundered on the border.

In the 2024 election, “immigration was playing a major, major role, and it was energizing Republicans. And it was the best issue among swing voters for Republicans,” she said. “ICE has gone too far, and that has backfired now.”

She added that the “best messaging” on immigration is “some control for the border plus a humanitarian process for immigration.”

Iowa’s Democratic Senate candidate Josh Turek traveled more than 800 miles to Laredo, Texas, to film an ad at the border touting his support for tougher enforcement.

“I came to the border to meet firsthand with the people who work to keep it secure. What happens down here affects us up in Iowa, so we’ve got to address it,” Turek says in the ad. “I voted with Republicans to allow law enforcement to arrest and deport criminals.”

Weeks earlier, he released another ad speaking to Iowans and vowing that he would “work with anyone” to fix immigration — “including President Trump, to secure the border.”

Closer to the border, Democrat Johnny Garcia is trying to win Texas’ redrawn and Republican-friendly 35th Congressional District against GOP nominee Carlos De La Cruz.

Garcia criticized Trump’s ICE raids as detrimental to the economy. But at a recent forum, he also blamed Biden’s policies for failures at the border and referred to a fatal smuggling conspiracy in 2022 that led to the deaths of dozens of people.

“We’ve also gotten to see, unfortunately, how Biden got it wrong on the border,” Garcia said. “I’ll admit that every single day. We got to see one of the largest migrant fatalities in this district in south San Antonio, with 53 migrants that were locked in a trailer.”

“So we can’t afford to just turn a blind eye to our border,” he added. “But at the same time, we can’t turn a blind eye to what we’re seeing happening on our streets.”

World.title: Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream for franchise’s first WNBA title
World.content:
In only their second season in existence, the Golden State Valkyries are WNBA champions.

The Valkyries won their first title in franchise history on Saturday, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. Forward Gabby Williams led with 30 points.

Confetti rained down onto the court as the crowd erupted in cheers, and the Valkyries celebrated the historic victory.

“I love moments like this,” Williams said after the final buzzer. “Nat told me to be patient in the first half. It was hard, but I listened to her. She’s right as always and she got us here,” she said referring to head coach Natalie Nakase.

Williams was named the Finals MVP following her stunning performance, scoring more points than anybody in a half in WNBA post-season history. Though she scored just two points in the first half, she rallied with 15 points in the third quarter and 13 in the fourth.

Accepting her award, she said, “I wasn’t gonna lose on Halloween.”

World.title: Judge dismisses Trump’s $10 billion defamation suit over Jeffrey Epstein birthday card story
World.content:
A federal judge in Florida has tossed a revised version of President Donald Trump’s $10 billion defamation suit against The Wall Street Journal over a story about a birthday card he allegedly sent Jeffrey Epstein more than two decades ago.

U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles found Trump’s amended suit suffered from the same fatal flaw as his first attempt — it fell far short of the high legal bar to show the paper had published the story with “actual malice.”

“As President Trump has not plausibly alleged that each Defendant made defamatory statements with actual malice, the Amended Complaint must be dismissed. And because this is President Trump’s second attempt to allege his claims, the Court finds that dismissal with prejudice is appropriate,” the judge wrote.

Trump first sued the paper last July, shortly after the Journal published a story about a birthday book that Ghislaine Maxwell had assembled for Epstein’s 50th birthday in 2003. The book appeared to include a card from Trump, who had been friends with Epstein around that time.

The card contained a hand-drawn outline of a naked woman with what appeared to be Trump’s first name signed in the pubic area. It included a typewritten note depicting an imaginary conversation with Epstein, who would later be charged with sex trafficking.

Trump denied having anything to do with the card, and his suit accused the paper of having made it up and that no such note existed.

Jeffrey Epstein in Cambridge, Mass., in 2004. Rick Friedman / Corbis via Getty Images file

Epstein’s estate later released a copy of a card matching the Journal’s description. Trump and the White House maintain the document is a fake.

Trump’s suit alleged the writers of the article “falsely represent as fact that President Trump drew the naked woman’s breasts and signed his name ‘Donald’ below her waist, ‘mimicking pubic hair,’” and that the article caused him “overwhelming financial and reputational harm.”

Trump’s suit also criticized the paper for not publishing an image of the card in the initial story, saying that shows “no authentic letter or drawing exists” — even though the House Oversight Committee publicly released the card after getting it from the Epstein estate.

The suit says the Journal should have known the story was bogus because Trump said it was not true. It also chided the paper for failing to interview Epstein co-conspirator Maxwell, who’s serving 20 years in prison on sex trafficking charges. The story said Journal reporters wrote her a letter asking for an interview and included a comment from her attorney.

The paper’s attorneys argued that like the original suit, Trump’s revised suit came “nowhere close” to demonstrating the paper acted with actual malice, in which “the false statement was made with knowledge that it was false or with reckless disregard of whether it was false or not.”

Despite Trump’s claim the paper failed to properly investigate the card before publishing the story, “the Article itself established that the Journal not only investigated” but also “informed readers that President Trump decried the Letter as a fake and denied writing it,” the paper said in its motion to dismiss the suit.

Further, the attorneys argued, alleging that someone sent another person a birthday card is not defamatory.

“There is nothing inherently defamatory about sending a bawdy letter to a friend,” the attorneys wrote, and the article “emphasizes that the Birthday Book was created before Epstein was first arrested” and “makes clear that President Trump’s friendship with Epstein ended years before Epstein was charged with sex crimes.”

The attorneys also contended the suit should be dismissed because the public release of the card shows the story was “substantially true.”

In an interview last year with then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche, Maxwell acknowledged assembling the birthday book but said she could not remember whether Trump contributed to it.

The White House maintains the signature is not Trump’s and that it looks different from his distinctive full signature. Democrats compiled a number of documents where Trump signed just his first name over the year, and the signatures appear very similar to the one on the card.

World.title: ‘Looks like Mars’: Toxic smog from Indonesia wildfires sparks health crisis, protests
World.content:
Almost every day for months, Indonesian schoolteacher Natanael Undas has gazed up at smoke-filled skies in apocalyptic shades of yellow and orange.

“It looks like Mars, like we’re living on another planet,” said Undas, whose home in central Kalimantan province is at the heart of devastating wildfires generating toxic smog in Indonesia and across Southeast Asia.

Although his family keeps the windows shut at all times, the noxious smoke penetrates the house anyway, sending Undas’ 2-year-old daughter into constant sneezing fits amid a spike in respiratory illnesses in haze-affected regions.

Wildfires are nothing new in Indonesia, whose forests and peatlands are set ablaze each year as family and commercial farms clear land using traditional “slash and burn” methods. But the fires this year are far worse than usual, said Undas, who has been documenting Indonesia’s air quality on Instagram since 2014, as heat and drought aggravated by a “super” El Niño weather pattern make this the country’s worst fire season in over a decade.

00:36 Wildfire smoke covers Indonesia skies in orange haze 00:00 00:00

The unrelenting haze from the fires has affected millions of people in the region since they started in July, closing schools in multiple countries and spurring arguments about who is to blame. Indonesian protesters have accused their government of insufficient action, while other countries are threatening prosecution.

On Wednesday, hundreds of Indonesian students and members of civil society groups protested in the capital, Jakarta, and other cities against the policies of President Prabowo Subianto, including his resistance to declaring the fires a national disaster.

“We want transparent and independent investigations about these wildfires,” protester Natasha Ruvantina told NBC News. “And also, we want a long-term prevention strategy.”

The Indonesian government said in a statement Wednesday that it recognized the students’ concerns, adding that it was prosecuting companies linked to the fires and sending aid to affected provinces.

The fires have also caused frustration in countries such as neighboring Singapore, where air pollution this month reached its highest level since 2015, when Indonesian wildfires were also intensified by El Niño. Singapore officials have threatened to prosecute companies seen as responsible for the devastation, and on Tuesday the foreign ministers of Singapore and Indonesia said they were considering a joint task force to combat illegal land burning.

“We will use the full force of the law to make sure those who profit from fire must answer for the fires,” Indonesian Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir said.

Indonesia’s neighbors and other countries have been accused of contributing to the problem.

In a report this month, the Indonesian environmental organization Walhi named 66 companies with links to Singapore and 27 companies with links to Malaysia that it said were associated with fire hot spots. On Thursday, the Indonesian government said police had identified 20 corporations suspected of being involved in the fires, including four from Singapore, Malaysia and South Korea.

World.title: Massive protests sweep Europe over cost of living and strained public services
World.content:
Massive protests were sweeping Europe on Saturday as part of demonstrations driven by the cost of living and deficient public services, with police bracing for potential violence after recent looting and riots.

Germany, France, Spain and Italy are among the nations where demonstrations were being held on Halloween following a recent wave of Gen Z-led marches across the continent.

French officials said they would deploy 70,000 police on Saturday following some of the worst rioting in decades, which erupted in cities across the country after student protests about the state of education evolved into wider demonstrations about the cost of living and social security.

A protester dressed in a unicorn costume faces police in riot gear in Cologne, Germany, on Saturday. Thilo Schmuelgen / Reuters

As the demonstrations began Saturday afternoon in Paris, protesters were pictured holding a banner that read: “We do not need tear gas for our future to be blurry.”

Videos vetted by NBC News show large crowds and fires burning in Marseille.

Some 320,000 people demonstrated across France on Saturday, including 70,000 in Paris, according to the French Interior Ministry. Authorities reported more than 560 arrests nationwide by Saturday night.

While the protests have been largely peaceful, police arrested 1,300 people last week after an estimated 410,000 took to the streets in cities across the country. Stores, public buildings and businesses have also been damaged since the protests erupted last month.

“Everyone is ​on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble,” Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said at a news conference earlier this week as he set out security arrangements, adding there was “a very high ⁠risk” of unrest.

Measures introduced last week to protect shops would be reinforced, he said, and demonstrations would not be permitted “in city centers, where there is a risk of public disorder.”

World.title: Heidi Klum reveals a giant severed hand as 2026 Halloween costume
World.content:
Heidi Klum underwent a bloody transformation to become a giant, gruesome severed hand for her annual Halloween party in New York on Saturday, 25 years after she began hosting the much-anticipated event.

Klum was unrecognizable, with only her eyes and mouth showing, blood dripping from her mouth as she stuck her tongue out. The top of the hand ended in a gory assortment of dangling ligaments and tendons. She had an ensemble of helpers in blood-stained hazmat suits.

The idea came to her last year to be a giant hand - specifically her own left hand, with long red nails, a thumb ring, and her engagement ring and wedding band.

Heidi Klum attends her 25th Annual Halloween Party at Cathédrale on October 31, 2026 in New York City. Noam Galai/Getty

Heidi Klum said this year's costume was modelled after her own left hand. Noam Galai/Getty

"I looked at my hand and I thought, 'Hey, I think I could fit my body in this somehow,'" Klum said.

The supermodel-turned-TV personality went viral in 2022 when she arrived at the party on the end of a fishing line, encased in a slithering worm costume.

In past years, Klum has come dressed as the Greek myth Medusa, a peacock, an 8-foot-tall (2.4-meter-tall) "Transformer," a werewolf from Michael Jackson's "Thriller" music video, a clone accompanied by several Klum-lookalikes, and Kali, the multiarmed Hindu goddess of death and destruction.

Heidi Klum attends Heidi Klum's 24th annual Halloween party at Hard Rock Hotel New York on Friday, Oct. 31, 2025, in New York. Photo by CJ Rivera/Invision/AP

Klum said it took about five to six hours to get into her hand costume this year, but making it took a lot longer. She posted hints on her Instagram earlier in the day as bloodied prosthetics were applied to her face.

"Hands down, the hardest thing is carrying it," Klum said. "It's quite heavy."

Her husband, musician Tom Kaulitz, did not attend this year because he was on tour. But the details on her costume include a tattoo of his name on her ring finger, along with her palm lines and veins.

"A little bit of Tom is with me," she said.
