Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday extended greetings to the people of Haryana as the state marked 60 years since its formation, praising its rich cultural heritage, sporting achievements and contributions to the country's growth.In a message posted on X, PM Modi highlighted Haryana's glorious history, courage and vibrant rural traditions, noting that its folk culture has played an important role in enriching India's cultural identity."Heartiest congratulations and best wishes to all my family members of the state on Haryana Day! Our state, adorned with a glorious history, remarkable valor, and a rich culture, is the pride of the nation. The folk traditions and vibrant rural culture here have always enriched the nation's cultural heritage," the Prime Minister wrote.PM Modi also acknowledged the contributions of Haryana's athletes and farmers, saying they have brought recognition to the country on international platforms and strengthened its food security."The people of Haryana have proven their talent and determination from agriculture, sports, and defence services to industry, education, and startups through their hard work and dedication.The athletes here are enhancing the honour of the tricolour, while the food providers are strengthening the country's food security. I wish that this special occasion brings prosperity into the lives of all the people here," he added.Union home minister Amit Shah also conveyed his wishes to Haryana's residents, describing the state as a land of courage, hard work and prosperity. In his message on X, he highlighted its contributions to national security, sports, agriculture and animal husbandry."Heartfelt greetings to all the residents of the state on the Foundation Day of Haryana, the land of valor, labour, and prosperity. Be it defending the nation on the borders, enhancing the honour of the tricolour on the sports fields, or setting new benchmarks in agriculture and animal husbandry, Haryana's contribution in every field is unparalleled," Amit Shah wrote.He further praised the state's soldiers, sportspersons and farmers for their role in strengthening India's reputation and economic progress, expressing hope that Haryana would continue to advance.Leader of the opposition in the lok sabha Rahul Gandhi also extended greetings to people across several states and union territories celebrating their foundation days on November 1.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi highlighted the country's diverse cultural traditions, languages and regional identities, saying they have shaped India's national character. He wished the regions continued prosperity and progress while contributing to a united nation.The Congress party also issued greetings to residents of Haryana and other states and Union territories marking their formation anniversaries. It called for continued progress, unity and commitment to constitutional values.At the state level, chief minister Nayab Singh Saini attended the foundation day celebrations in Chandigarh, marking six decades since Haryana became a separate state on November 1, 1966.Recalling the state's journey, Saini acknowledged the contributions of those who had campaigned for its formation and worked towards its development."We express our gratitude to all the great personalities who struggled for the formation of Haryana and worked hard for the construction of modern Haryana. On this day in 1966, when it became a separate state, it was very backward. Our farmer benefactors, hardworking labourers, diligent industrialists and traders, and valiant sportspersons all made a significant contribution in transforming that backward region into a modern, developed Haryana," the chief minister said.Haryana, Karnataka, Kerala, Punjab and Tamil Nadu observe their state formation day on November 1. Several union territories, including Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Lakshadweep, also mark their foundation day on the occasion.

World.title: Fat-dissolving claims land FatX Solution in regulatory trouble; CDSCO cancels registration
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Promising to dissolve fat cells may sound like an attractive pitch for a slimming product, but it has landed FatX Solution in trouble with the country's drug regulator.

The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has cancelled the product's registration after finding that it was being promoted with claims that are not permitted for cosmetics.

In an order dated October 28, CDSCO said Delhi-based importer Tekno Midas Aesthetics was marketing FatX Solution on its website as a product that could dissolve fat cells and reduce their size. The regulator said these were drug-related claims and did not fit the definition of a cosmetic under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

The action followed a scrutiny of the company's application and website, during which CDSCO found differences between the claims being made online and those mentioned on the approved product label.

Under the Cosmetics Rules, 2020, cosmetic products cannot make false or misleading claims. The rules define cosmetics as products meant for cleansing, beautifying, promoting attractiveness or altering appearance.





Claims to dissolve fat cells go beyond this definition, the regulator said.

CDSCO had issued a show-cause notice to the company on August 10, citing violations of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and the Cosmetics Rules. The company submitted its response on September 1, but the regulator found it inconclusive and unsatisfactory. The firm also requested that its registration certificate be voluntarily surrendered.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Rajan Bhatnagar of Tekno Midas Aesthetics told TOI that the product had been registered as a cosmetic more than four years ago. "At that time, the licence was granted because the product was registered as a cosmetic. The authorities have now changed their interpretation of the category under which the product falls. Earlier, it was considered a cosmetic, but now they say it falls under another category," he said.

He said the company had decided not to contest the matter after receiving the notice. "We did not want to get into any dispute or challenge the notification. We voluntarily requested the surrender of the licence, and the authorities cancelled it," he said.

The Central Licensing Authority subsequently cancelled the registration certificate, RC/COS-003300, which was issued in July 2022 and was valid until July 14, 2027. The cancellation took effect from October 28.

World.title: ‘It was Nehru Ji’s chair’: Cong reveals significance of seat used by Meira Kumar during CEC’s public impeachment
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Lok Sabha Speaker

presided over the INDIA bloc's symbolic âpublic impeachmentâ of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday, seated in a chair steeped in history. The chair was once used by India's first Prime Minister

.

The information was shared by Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera, who was involved in organising the event at the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at 10, Rajaji Marg in New Delhi.

âThe chair on which Meira Kumar sat during today's public impeachment proceedings against the CEC was once occupied by the first prime minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, the great-grandfather of Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi,â Khera later said in a post on X.

âIt was Nehru Ji's chair throughout his tenure as prime minister. It witnessed some of the most consequential decisions in our nation's history and carries the weight of that legacy,â he added.

Khera said that Meira Kumar, sitting in the same chair, pronounced Gyanesh Kumar âunfit to continue as the Chief Election Commissioner of Indiaâ.

âGyanesh Kumar has been rejected by the people of India. It is only a matter of time before he goes,â he said.





The INDIA bloc organised the symbolic proceedings, accusing the CEC of allegedly facilitating the deletion of voters' names from electoral rolls and demanding that he be tried in court for treason and jailed.

Kumar opened the proceedings, saying the opposition had decided to convene the meeting because of alleged wrongful deletions of eligible voters.

âWhen this issue is raised by the INDIA bloc, there is no accountability.

So we have decided that the INDIA bloc will hold a meeting and bring a proposal to remove Gyanesh Kumar,â she said.

The resolution was moved by Kharge, seconded by Samajwadi Party leader Harendra Malik and supported by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition MPs and civil society representatives. It was adopted unanimously through a show of hands.

Kharge alleged that the right to vote was under threat and accused the Election Commission of functioning at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah.

Rahul Gandhi described the proceedings as a âpolitical weaponâ against those who, he alleged, had colluded to destroy people's votes.

The BJP criticised the event, accusing the INDIA bloc of making a âmockeryâ of Parliament and democracy.

World.title: ‘Don’t just protest, shop’: Rahul urges INDIA bloc rally to support Delhi traders
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As thousands of people gathered at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on Sunday for the INDIA blocâs âChalo Dilliâ rally, Congress leader

urged participants to support local traders by shopping from their stores during the festive season.

His appeal came after tradersâ associations opposed the November 1 rally, warning that the gathering could disrupt business in the capitalâs key commercial markets.

In a video message posted on X late on Saturday, Gandhi appealed to people travelling to Delhi from different parts of the country to support small businesses by purchasing goods after attending the rally. He said the gathering would not hurt traders and accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of spreading rumours about its economic impact.

âTomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March. It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here,â Gandhi said.

âProtest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders,â he added.

Reiterating his appeal, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha said: âI know the rally will not harm the traders.





The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours.â

âBut let's do both. Tomorrow there will be a march, there will be a rally, and lakhs of people will buy goods from the small shops of our traders,â he said, while extending Diwali greetings.

Traders flag festive-season business losses

Gandhi's appeal follows representations by the Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) and the Federation of Sadar Bazar Traders Association, which had urged him and Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi to defer the November 1 rally until after the festive season.

âWe demand to reschedule the mega-rally of 1 million (10 lakh) people, planned for November 1, to a date after Diwali; lack of parking for 15,000â20,000 vehicles could lead to a total gridlock, akin to a lockdown,â the traders' body said.

World.title: Uttarakhand chopper crash: Mortal remains of all six victims recovered, sent to Rishikesh AIIMS
World.content:
The mortal remains of all six people who died in the helicopter crash near Joshimath in Uttarakhand were recovered and sent to AIIMS, Rishikesh, on Sunday (November 1, 2026) morning, the Chamoli district administration said.

On Friday (October 30), the chopper crashed on a hillside near Chai village in Joshimath while it was returning to Dehradun from the Badrinath shrine.

The mortal remains were brought to the Community Health Centre (CHC), Joshimath, by road. Officials said that after completing the necessary formalities, the mortal remains were sent to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Rishikesh, by helicopter.

The district administration said that teams of the Indian Army, ITBP, SDRF, NDRF, police, district administration and the Forest Department jointly conducted the search operation amidst challenging conditions in the inaccessible and high-altitude hilly area.

"The bodies of all six deceased were taken out by rescue teams on foot on difficult mountain paths," mentions a statement issued by the district administration on Sunday (November 1).

The operation started on Friday (October 30) after the chopper crashed, but due to the difficult terrain and remote location, it took over 24 hours for teams to complete the operation.

World.title: Mysuru City Corporation collects ₹210 crore in property tax so far this year: Yathindra Siddaramaiah
World.content:
Minister in charge of Mysuru district Yathindra Siddaramaiah said the Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) has collected ₹210 crore in property tax so far during the current financial year.

He was delivering his Rajyothsava Day address in Mysuru on Sunday (November 1, 2026). It may be mentioned here that the MCC had set a target of collecting ₹286.72 crore in property tax during 2026-27.

During his address, Mr. Yathindra said a special ‘Prajaseva’ e-Khata campaign by charging a nominal fee of just ₹175 had been organised by MCC recently. During the campaign, over 590 property owners had been distributed e-khata documents within 72 hours of submitting their applications.

So far, around 78,000 ‘A’ and ‘B’ Khatas have been issued in MCC, he added.

GRAMANUBHAVA: Mr. Yathindra also launched the ‘Gramanubhava’ or Village Experience programme, an initiative by the State Government’s Department of School Education and Literacy aimed at creating awareness among urban students about rural life, agricultural culture, and their connection to the soil.

AWARDS: Meanwhile, a total of 92 persons were given away district level Rajyothsava awards on the occasion.

Also, SSLC and PUC students who studied in the Kannada medium at Government schools and secured the high marks were felicitated.

Narasimharaja Assembly constituency MLA Tanveer Sait, MLCs C.N. Manjegowda and Raghu, Deputy Commissioner G. Lakshmikanth Reddy, Zilla Panchayat CEO S. Yukesh Kumar, Mysuru City Police Commissioner Seema Latkar, Mysuru City Corporation Commissioner M.K. Savitha, Additional Deputy Commissioner R. Aishwarya along with other officials, pro-Kannada activists, and dignitaries were present at the event.

World.title: Foolish drama, will be final nail in coffin of Congress' political future: Nadda
World.content:
Union Minister J.P. Nadda on Sunday (November 1, 2026) slammed the Opposition INDIA bloc's rally as a "foolish and designed drama" and said it will prove to be the final "nail in the coffin" of Congress' "political downfall".

Mr. Nadda alleged that the protest was part of a well-thought-out conspiracy to surrender democracy to anarchy and disorder.

INDIA block protest rally at Ramlila Maidan LIVE updates

In an apparent reference to the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, Mr. Nadda claimed that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's objective behind organising it on Sunday was to rub salt into the wounds of "Sikh brothers".

"Removing the democratically elected government by conspiring to spread riots and anarchy in Delhi, adversely impacting the earnings of shopkeepers and traders in Delhi during the festive season and defaming the country are other objectives of the rally," the senior BJP leader told reporters.

"The day of November 1 is the ugliest and darkest blot on India's democratic history. On this very day, goons patronised by Congress massacred our innocent Sikh brothers. Thousands and lakhs of Sikh families became homeless overnight."

Mr. Nadda said India is a strong democracy and will not be run by riot-based politics, but by the Constitution and the mandate of the people.

“Whatever is happening today at Ramlila Maidan is not respect for democracy, but a well-thought-out conspiracy to surrender democracy to anarchy and disorder.

"This is a foolish and designed drama of people who have been defeated and repeatedly rejected by the public. The public understands this very well,” he charged.

The Opposition alliance is holding the 'Chalo Dilli' protest in the national capital as part of its campaign against alleged electoral irregularities and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

"Rahul Gandhi, listen carefully. You cannot hide the dark history of November 1. You cannot escape answering for the tears of Delhi's traders," Mr. Nadda said, adding, "Your rally will prove to be the final nail in the coffin of Congress' political downfall."

World.title: Anantapur chainsaw attack: A.P. Minister Nara Lokesh says Class 10 girl stable after bleeding controlled
World.content:
The Class 10 student from Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu, who was attacked with an electric chainsaw on Saturday (October 31, 2026), has been stabilised and receiving significant medical care at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.

Andhra Pradesh Education Minister and Human Resources Development Minister Nara Lokesh, who is closely monitoring the situation, updated the victim’s medical condition on X. In the latest post, he said that the medical team at Manipal Hospital stabilised the girl’s condition with blood transfusions and supportive treatment.

“Doctors have successfully controlled the major bleeding in the OT. The child’s BP is now being maintained,” Mr. Lokesh said. He appreciated all the doctors, medical teams and officials who worked tirelessly in coordinating the emergency care.

Update from Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru: The medical team stabilised the condition with blood transfusions and supportive treatment. Doctors have successfully controlled the major bleeding in the OT. The child's BP is now being maintained. Our sincere appreciation to all the doctors, medical teams and officials who worked tirelessly in coordinating the emergency care. The child continues to receive close medical attention. We remain hopeful for a full recovery. — Lokesh Nara (@naralokesh) October 31, 2026

“The child continues to receive close medical attention. We remain hopeful for a full recovery,” he said.

Meanwhile, Mr. Lokesh is likely to reach Bengaluru today to consult the medical team about the girl’s condition and meet the victim’s family to assure them of support for her recovery.

World.title: Israeli protesters demand opposition ally with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu
World.content:
Hundreds of Israelis took to the streets on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to urge the opposition to ally with Arab parties to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has gone on the offensive against the minority group's leaders.

Arab-majority parties made major gains in Tuesday’s election, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them.

Joining a rally in Tel Aviv, Ayelet Raz said that the Arab community, which accounts for around 20% of Israel's population, had a right to political participation.

"It's the last chance for real change," the 60-year-old psychologist said, warning that Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, was a "great manipulator".

"We need to give peace a chance," she said. "Otherwise we'll have this bloodshed forever."

Tuesday’s election was inconclusive, with neither bloc reaching a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament.

Jewish-majority parties opposed to Mr. Netanyahu, known by his nickname Bibi, won 48 seats, while two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats.

An alliance between the two camps would potentially give the anti-Netanyahu bloc a comfortable majority of 67 seats, but the idea is opposed by some parties in the opposition bloc.

"Arabs and Jews will only win together" and "There is a majority for change" read some of the signs held by around 500 protesters in Tel Aviv.

"67 — United we stand, divided we get Bibi" and "Why not, really — unless we are racist?" read some of the placards at the 100-strong rally in Jerusalem.

Arab parties have only once formally sat in an Israeli government, when Raam leader Mansour Abbas joined a short-lived coalition that lasted from 2021 to 2022. He has voiced a willingness to do so again.

The Joint List's Yousef Jabareen, meanwhile, has told AFP he is willing to support Mr. Eisenkot in parliament without joining his government, citing, among other concerns, the war in Gaza.

Opposition division

Mr. Eisenkot, 66, a former military chief and political novice, largely shares Mr. Netanyahu's views on security issues including Gaza, which Israel has reduced to rubble since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023.

Mr. Eisenkot reiterated on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that he would only form a "Zionist government" whose members commit to the "recognition of Israel as a Jewish, democratic and liberal state" and to the "recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organisation", conditions that Arab leaders have previously refused to accept.

While he has said he does not want a government dependent on Arab lists, Mr. Eisenkot has not explicitly rejected their external support.

"I want them (the opposition bloc) to go ahead to be brave and do the right thing," said demonstrator Sharon Balaban, 55, a video artist in Jerusalem.

Yair Golan, leader of the left-wing Democrats has enthusiastically supported the prospect of a government backed by Arab parties, saying it would be racist to exclude them, and on Thursday (October 29, 2026) met Mr. Abbas.

But Avigdor Liberman, leader of the right-wing anti-Netanyahu Yisrael Beitenu party, has said he will not enter a coalition that relies on Arab parties, even for external support.

"Whoever wants to rely on supporters of terrorism, let them. Yisrael Beiteinu will not be there," he wrote on Facebook on Friday (October 30, 2026).

Arabs ‘are for Hamas’

On the sidelines of the demonstration in Tel Aviv, more than 100 Netanyahu supporters staged a counter-protest.

"It's the Right, or Palestine," they chanted, repeating a slogan from Mr. Netanyahu's campaign.

"The two Arab parties are for Hamas", said Rebecca Schindler, 60. "They want to make Israel an Arab country."

Nava Rehavia, 70, called on Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Liberman to join a Netanyahu-led coalition and said: "The Arabs did not win, because they stole the election."

Mr. Netanyahu sought to raise allegations of electoral fraud during voting day, saying Arab parties had been caught with envelopes of cash.

Police said they had arrested three suspects, but the election commission described the incident as an isolated local case.

Mr. Netanyahu later raised allegations that Arab politicians improperly received support from Qatar.

Collaboration with Arab parties would be "a disaster for Israel", Mr. Netanyahu posted on social media on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

President Isaac Herzog is expected to grant a party leader a mandate to form a government within 28 days by Thursday (October 29, 2026), with a possible 14-day extension.

The negotiations come as Mr. Netanyahu and U.S. President Donald Trump have hinted at a new attack on Iran, which could help Mr. Netanyahu run out the clock until new elections.

World.title: Six Indian tourists stranded in Nepal, rescue efforts underway
World.content:
Security personnel are making efforts to rescue six Indian tourists, including two women, stranded due to heavy snowfall in the Shey-Phoksundo National Park area of Nepal since Saturday afternoon (October 31, 2026), officials said on Sunday (November 1, 2026).

The tourists had gone to the Dho area in Shey Phoksundo Rural Municipality’s Ward No. 8, which was covered in heavy snow, according to Dolpa Chief District Officer Junu Dhakal.

Shey Phoksundo Lake, located in the rural municipality, is Nepal’s deepest lake. It is situated at an altitude of 3,600 metres and has an estimated depth of 145 metres.

“We have located the area where they are stranded, and an Army helicopter is arriving to rescue them. We hope to rescue them soon,” Ms. Dhakal told PTI.

The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, she said.

Ms. Dhakal said the tourists left the guide and proceeded towards the lake area despite heavy snowfall. Communication with them was disrupted on Saturday night (October 31, 2026).

The guide contacted the District Administration Office in Dolpa on Saturday evening (October 31, 2026), saying the tourists might have been stranded due to heavy snowfall, she said. However, communication was completely disrupted on Sunday morning (November 1, 2026).

“We cannot say they are missing, as we have located the area,” Ms. Dhakal clarified.

The tourists have been identified as Moumita Halder, Piyali Koley, Jajla Trivedi Kumar, Aditya Singha, Diplina Bishwas and Rajesh De, according to a press release issued by the District Administration Office, Dolpa.

Security personnel are being mobilised, and a rescue helicopter is expected to arrive soon, the press release said.

World.title: Sonia, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee among INDIA bloc leaders marching to Ramlila Maidan, demanding CEC's removal | LIVE
World.content:
Senior INDIA bloc leaders, including Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and Mamata Banerjee, marched from Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence towards Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on Sunday (November 1, 2026) in an open bus, for the alliance’s rally demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities. Supporters have gathered at the venue and party workers at locations across the capital.

Posters announcing the INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Delhi’ march were put up outside Ramlila Maidan, as security personnel were deployed at the venue ahead of the Opposition’s mega rally on Sunday (November 1, 2026). A post by the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) also highlighted the rally, with preparations underway ahead of the event.

The bloc carried out a symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, unanimously adopting a motion by a show of hands on Saturday (October 31).

They levelled six charges against him, including conspiring with the ruling BJP to steal elections, deleting 13.2 crore voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter lists, and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.

World.title: US hears Pakistan’s concerns over terrorism from Afghanistan, would play ‘productive role’ if there is one: Rubio
World.content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Saturday said that Washington has “heard” Pakistan’s concerns about terrorism emanating from Afghanistan and if “there’s a productive role for us to play, we would play it”.

Rubio’s statement came in response to a question about tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan at a press talks in Atlanta.

“Pakistan is concerned about terrorist attacks that are being sponsored from the territory of Afghanistan. They feel as if the Taliban have not done enough to constrain those attacks, and they have taken action against it.

“We obviously have heard those concerns on their part. We obviously don’t want them to be targeted for terrorism. So if there’s a productive role for us to play, we would play it,” Rubio said.

Mentioning that the US did not “necessarily [have] the closest relationship” with the Afghan Taliban, Rubio added: “We’ve heard the concerns that Pakistan has raised and we’ve seen some of those attacks that they point to. We’re against terrorism no matter where it emanates from and who it targets.”

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), that it says are used for attacks in Pakistan.

For their part, the Afghan Taliban have avoided taking a categorical position on the TTP and other groups, while rejecting Islamabad’s allegations that Afghanistan is being used as a base for attacks against Pakistan.

On Saturday, Pakistan’s information ministry rebuked the Afghan Taliban’s stance on the ongoing conflict between the two countries, assailing its “persistent refusal to address terrorism” emanating from Afghanistan’s soil.

The statement came in response to remarks made by Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, who blamed Islamabad’s “wrong policies” for preventing a resolution to the conflict and insisted Kabul was not the cause of counterterrorism issues.

In its response, the information ministry said the Afghan spokesman’s remarks expose the “regime’s deeply misguided approach and unwillingness to confront the root cause of deteriorating relations with Pakistan”.

“The Taliban leadership continues to blame Islamabad’s policies while conveniently ignoring the single most important issue poisoning bilateral relations: its persistent failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil,” it added.

Islamabad reiterated that the “Taliban regime’s persistent refusal to address terrorism remains the principal obstacle to normal relations”.

Multiple rounds of talks between the two sides last year, facilitated by Qatar and Turkiye , failed to bring about any workable solution, with the Pakistani government saying the Taliban officials gave no assurances on the key issues. Efforts this year made with China’s involvement also resulted in no breakthrough.

Russia, the only country to have formally recognised the Taliban government, has also recently renewed its offer to facilitate a settlement if both sides request its involvement.

Moscow’s special envoy for Afghanistan, Zamir Kabulov, had last month made this suggestion after the latest round of the Moscow Format consultations on Oct 5 ended without a joint communiqué because of differences between Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban delegations over references to terrorist networks operating from Afghanistan.

When asked about it during a weekly media briefing, Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan had said talks with Afghanistan could not be unconditional. He also rejected suggestions that Islamabad was unwilling to engage with its neighbour, saying it would welcome sincere efforts by friendly countries to help resolve the dispute.

He further stated: “At present, I am not aware of any separate, formal Russian mediation initiative being under discussion.”

Meanwhile, intermittent skirmishes at the border continue.

September witnessed yet another bout of conflict between the two neighbours, with Pakistan carrying out calibrated airstrikes in the border region in response to terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

World.title: LPG price twice the official  rate in open market
World.content:
• Ogra notifies about Rs15 per kg increase in gas price

• Association warns of strike from Nov 16 over new LPG policy

ISLAMABAD: As the government again notified an increase in the price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for November, its price in the open market is twice as high as the official rate amid a shortage of LPG due to the US-Iran war.

In a notification on Saturday, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) notified Rs294,075 per tonne for November compared to Rs279,341 in the previous month. Following the increase, the official retail rate of an 11.8 kg domestic cylinder of LPG is Rs3,470, up by Rs173. The official LPG rate is Rs294 per kilogramme.

The oil and gas regulator said that the LPG producer price was linked with Saudi Aramco-CP and the US dollar exchange rate. It added that compared to the previous month, Saudi Aramco-CP had increased by 6.47 per cent, while the average dollar exchange rate had slightly decreased by 0.12pc, resulting in an increase in the LPG consumer price by Rs14.73 per kg.

In the open market, LPG is selling for up to Rs630 per kg, while the company-operated franchises are charging up to Rs400 per kg, with many warning that the crisis would compound due to the gas shortage.

LPG Distributors Association of Pakistan Chairman Irfan Khokhar said that the situation was serious because of the Iran border closure. He said at least 70 per cent of LPG was imported from Iran, while only 30pc was locally produced. “The government has to make serious efforts to control market manipulations,” Mr Khokhar added.

On the other hand, LPG marketing companies thre­atened to shut down their businesses from Nov 16 if the private sector was sidelined in the upcoming LPG policy. Pakistan LPG Marketers Association Cha­irman Ali Haider warned that they will observe a strike from Nov 16 if the government implemented the policy. He said the government should not reverse the deregulation of LPG, adding that the gas was in short supply due to the Iran border closure.

“Out of around 1.3 million tonnes, only around 225,000 is imported from the Gulf, and that too has been mainly imported by the private sector,” he said, adding that the ProGas terminal at Port Qasim was under the control of the Sui Southern Gas Company which “imported LPG around seven months back”. The association also wrote a letter to Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, stating the draft policy sent to the prime minister had no input from the private sector. The association called for the complete deregulation of the LPG sector.

It said the 2016 LPG policy imposed Rs4,669 per tonne petroleum development levy on locally produced LPG. This was imposed to provide subsidies to the state-owned entities such as the PSO, Parco, and SSGC to import LPG during winters and in any emergency, like the current scenario. “Despite billions of rupees collected in terms of PDL through this formula, the state-owned entities have failed to import LPG during these days,” Mr Haider alleged.

Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

World.title: Pakistan becomes chair of G-24 bloc of developing nations, reaffirms pledge to fairer global financial system
World.content:
Pakistan assumed the chairmanship of the Group of 24 (G-24) on Sunday, with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb expressing the country’s resolve to strengthen the collective voice of developing economies and “advancing a more responsive, fair and development-oriented international financial system”.

The intergovernmental group is a coalition of developing countries established in 1971 to coordinate their positions on international monetary and financial issues, according to its website.

Aurangzeb described the chairmanship as a “profound responsibility”, a handout issued by the Ministry of Finance stated, adding that he also called for “renewed international cooperation, stronger multilateral institutions and reinforced global commitments to address climate shocks, development financing gaps and global economic fragmentation”.

“The future of developing economies is not peripheral to the future of the global economy. It is central to it,” the statement quoted the finance minister as saying.

He further highlighted the “immense potential of emerging and developing nations as drivers of investment, innovation, entrepreneurship and global growth”.

Aurangzeb outlined three strategic priorities for Pakistan under the chairmanship: placing development at the centre of global economic policymaking, strengthening multilateral frameworks, and advancing a development-oriented international financial architecture.

For the first priority, the finance minister stressed the importance of macroeconomic stability, saying it must underpin investment, productivity, employment, and shared prosperity.

He added that such an approach would enable “developing and low-income economies to move beyond crisis management towards sustainable growth”.

Secondly, he added that under its chairmanship, Pakistan would advocate for “more equitable and fair governance, meaningful participation in decision-making and greater responsiveness of the Bretton Woods institutions to the evolving needs and realities of their members”.

Thirdly, the finance minister said Pakistan would prioritise affordable and timely development financing, sustainable debt solutions, stronger global financial safety nets, climate resilience, and greater mobilisation of public and private capital.

“Our task is to ensure that the immense potential of developing economies is not constrained by an international financial architecture that has yet to fully adapt to a changing world,” Aurangzeb was quoted as saying.

The finance minister emphasised aligning financial stability with long-term development objectives, drawing on Pakistan’s experience with economic stabilisation, reform and resilience, the statement said.

He added that this would ensure that reforming economies have the necessary financing and policy space to pursue sustainable growth.

Aurangzeb further stated that Pakistan’s tenure as the chair would be guided by “G-24’s longstanding principles of consultation, consensus and collective advocacy, working closely with members across Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, alongside the International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Bank and other international partners, to translate shared priorities into practical outcomes.”

According to the statement, the finance czar acknowledged outgoing chair Nigeria’s leadership and pledged to build on the group’s progress.

He further emphasised that the “effectiveness of collective leadership must be judged by tangible development outcomes”.

“The true measure of our collective leadership will not simply be the strength of our voice, but the difference that voice makes,” the ministry quoted him as saying.

According to the statement, Aurangzeb reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to advancing G-24’s mission “from collective voice to collective influence, and from collective influence to meaningful progress”.

The development comes as Pakistan was named the incoming chair of the Boards of Governors of the IMF and the World Bank Group (WBG) for next year, for the first time since 1953, last month.

PM hopes chairmanship will help Pakistan advocate for global financial reforms

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif welcomed the development, calling it a “significant diplomatic milestone” and went on to express hope that the chairmanship will provide Pakistan “an opportunity to play an influential role in advocating for necessary reforms within the global financial system, securing equitable financial support to address climate change, and promoting sustainable development opportunities for emerging economies”, a statement issued by his office said.

He also lauded the finance minister and his team for their “tireless efforts, effective diplomacy, and professional competence”.

The premier further commended the team for ensuring “impactful” participation at the recently held annual meetings of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which he said helped Pakistan secure a “prominent position in the economic leadership of developing nations”.

World.title: PIA resumes direct flights to China
World.content:
BEIJING: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has resumed its flight operations between Pakistan and China with the first flight operating on Oct 30, reconnecting Islamabad and Beijing through direct air services.

The resumption marks a significant milestone in strengthening aviation links between the two countries and reflects PIAs commitment to restoring and maintaining regular operations in the Chinese market.

Under the renewed schedule, PIA will operate weekly flights between Islamabad and Beijing every Friday, providing passengers with a direct and convenient travel option between the two capitals. The airline also aims to offer competitive fares while ensuring consistent and reliable services.

In a major step towards expanding its network across China, PIA has strengthened its cooperation with three leading Chinese airlines — Air China, Shenzhen Airlines and Hainan Airlines.

Through its partnership with Air China, passengers will benefit from onward connections to various domestic destinations through Beijing, a major aviation hub.

World.title: Binance to resume withdrawals after covering bulk of stolen $6.3bn
World.content:
Binance, the worlds biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said it would resume withdrawals on Sunday after covering 95 per cent of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from its platform in the world’s largest digital heist, which the FBI has tied to North Korea.

The exchange, founded in China, said the first phase of withdrawals would start between 0600 and 0900 GMT and cover 15 crypto assets including bitcoin, ether, XRP, dogecoin and others.

Binance said on Sunday it had covered $6bn of stolen cryptocurrencies by using company money to buy replacement tokens. The remaining 5pc of stolen tokens consist of assets that are less liquid and may take longer to source in the required amounts, according to the exchange.

FBI ties attack to North Korea unit

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts.

Last year, attackers stole $2.9bn worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.

The FBI said on Saturday the North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack.

Pyongyang has for years denied using state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment.

Law enforcement observed members of the unit converting stolen assets into the cryptocurrency ether, the FBI said in a statement, adding that it expected “further laundering” of the assets through the use of related technology.

Analysts had blamed North Korea and said the Binance theft could be the largest financial heist of all time.

The bulk of the theft unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.

US President Donald Trump, however, said on Saturday that the US was still not certain if North Korea was involved.

“We don’t know if it’s North Korea but if it is, we’ll talk to North Korea about it,” Trump told reporters on Saturday in comments posted by a White House handle on X.

Binance vows to bear financial costs

Binance has been working with industry partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3bn located as of Friday, it said.

The exchange has repeatedly said it would bear the financial impact of the funds stolen in the hack. It has set aside around $6.34bn of company funds internally to cover the losses.

The money spent buying replacement tokens came from Binance’s $1bn Secure Asset Fund for Users( Safu), a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some of its Futures Insurance Fund and its corporate treasury, it said on X.

Co-CEO Yi He said on Saturday that 50pc of its Safu funds would be used, while the company committed to replenishing the fund to about $1 bn.

Richard Teng, the other co-CEO, has said that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it harder to trace and investigate.

Crypto prices fell on Friday, while Binance sought to reassure customers that their funds were safe after the hack.

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.

World.title: Islamabad High Court bars FIR mention in character certificates after acquittal
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that police cannot mention an FIR in the character certificate of a citizen who has been acquitted in the case, declaring any such certificate unlawful and invalid.

Justice Ayyaz Shaukat, while deciding a public interest petition, directed the Inspector General of Police, Islamabad, to establish a formal mechanism to ensure that references to criminal cases ending in acquittal are not included in character certificates issued to citizens.

The court observed that citizens should not be compelled to approach courts to exercise rights already guaranteed under the law.

It held that following an acquittal, there was no legal justification for portraying an individual as an accused or criminal through a police-issued character certificate.

Rules such mention violates constitutional rights, including dignity and freedom of movement

Allowing the petition, the court ordered the removal of a reference to an FIR registered at Shalimar Police Station from the petitioner’s character certificate.

The judgement clarified that although police could maintain internal records of criminal cases for official purposes, such information could not be disclosed in character certificates issued to citizens, particularly when these were required for travelling abroad.

It further observed that there was no legal basis for mentioning an FIR in a character certificate after the proceedings had culminated in a final acquittal. Any certificate containing such a reference would be legally invalid.

Justice Ayyaz Shaukat also rejected the police’s description of the petitioner as having been “discharged” during the investigation, observing that such a characterisation undermined the legal effect and status of the acquittal.

The court held that including an FIR in a character certificate despite an individual’s acquittal violated Articles 4, 9, 14 and 15 of the Constitution, which protect citizens’ rights, liberty, dignity and freedom of movement.

It emphasised that a person acquitted through due process of law could not continue to face adverse consequences through a character certificate suggesting involvement in criminal proceedings.

The court directed the Islamabad police chief to introduce a proper procedure to ensure that acquitted citizens did not have to initiate fresh litigation merely to obtain character certificates reflecting their actual legal status.

Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

World.title: US to deport 150 Afghan immigrants back to Kabul
World.content:
WASHINGTON: President Don­­ald Trump’s administration plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan via Pakistan, US media reported, a move advocacy groups say could endanger their lives.

Trump last year issued travel bans for a number of countries, including Afghanistan, as part of a broad immigration crackdown, and sought to end deportation protections for Afghans, some of whom were granted special immigrant visas following the August 2021 takeover by the Taliban.

More than 150 Afghan immigrants are expected to be deported in the latest push, The New York Times reported on Friday, citing three unnamed US officials, and the first flight could leave as soon as Monday.

Among those expected to be deported are relatives of Afghans who assisted the US military in the country prior to the fall of Kabul, according to AfghanEvac, a group seeking to help former Afghan allies.

While the US cannot arrange deportations directly to Afgha­n­istan, the officials told the Times that Pakistan will oversee their expulsion to Afghanistan.
